registers.name: MATRIX_MCFGx
registers.title: Bus Matrix Host Configuration Registers
notes: Writable only while WPEN is 0 in MATRIX_WPMR.

fields.name: ULBT
fields.text: Chooses how an undefined-length (INCR) burst from this host is split for re-arbitration.

values.name: UNLTD_LENGTH
values.text: No end of burst is predicted: an INCR burst breaks only at the client's slot cycle limit, otherwise ending at the latest on the next 1-Kbyte AHB boundary (up to 256 word or 128 double-word beats). Not for a host that issues back-to-back undefined-length bursts to one client, which could lock that client's arbitration and shut other hosts out.

values.name: SINGLE_ACCESS
values.text: Each beat of the INCR burst is handled as a single access, so arbitration can occur on every beat.

values.name: 4BEAT_BURST
values.text: Split into bursts of at most 4 beats; re-arbitration every 4 beats.

values.name: 8BEAT_BURST
values.text: Split into bursts of at most 8 beats; re-arbitration every 8 beats.

values.name: 16BEAT_BURST
values.text: Split into bursts of at most 16 beats; re-arbitration every 16 beats.

values.name: 32BEAT_BURST
values.text: Split into bursts of at most 32 beats; re-arbitration every 32 beats.

values.name: 64BEAT_BURST
values.text: Split into bursts of at most 64 beats; re-arbitration every 64 beats.

values.name: 128BEAT_BURST
values.text: Split into bursts of at most 128 beats; re-arbitration every 128 beats. Leaving ULBT at its reset value 0 saves power unless another setting is needed.

registers.name: MATRIX_SCFGx
registers.title: Bus Matrix Client Configuration Registers
notes: For clients 2 and 3 the reset value is 0x0002_01FF, so DEFMSTR_TYPE resets to 2 (FIXED).
Writable only while WPEN is 0 in MATRIX_WPMR.

fields.name: FIXED_DEFMSTR
fields.text: Number of this client's default host, used only when DEFMSTR_TYPE is 2; a host not connected to this client acts as DEFMSTR_TYPE 0.

fields.name: DEFMSTR_TYPE
fields.text: Chooses which host, if any, this client stays connected to when idle.

values.name: NONE
values.text: With no other host request pending at the end of an access, the client disconnects from all hosts, adding one clock cycle of latency to the first access of a burst or to a single access.

values.name: LAST
values.text: With no other host request pending at the end of an access, the client stays connected to the host that used it last, so that host's next access has no added cycle of latency.

values.name: FIXED
values.text: With no other host request pending at the end of an access, the client connects to the host numbered in FIXED_DEFMSTR, so that host's next access has no added cycle of latency.

fields.name: SLOT_CYCLE
fields.text: Number of AHB clock cycles after the last arbitration before a new one is held; a pending request from another host then breaks the current burst. 0 turns the limit off, so bursts complete unless split by ULBT. Too small a value cuts every burst, leaving the matrix busy arbitrating with no data moved; the reset maximum is usually a safe choice. The limit serves host latency needs; in most cases it is not needed and is to be turned off to save power.

fields.name: FARG
fields.text: Argument of the Flash command. GETD, GLB, GGPB, STUI, SPUI, GCALB, WUS, EUS, STUS, SPUS and EA take none and FARG is written 0. ES: any page number inside the sector to erase. EPA: FARG[1:0] sets the page count and the start page goes in FARG[15:2]; 0 = 4 pages, FARG[15:2] = page/4; 1 = 8 pages, FARG[15:3] = page/8, FARG[2] = 0; 2 = 16 pages, FARG[15:4] = page/16, FARG[3:2] = 0; 3 = 32 pages, FARG[15:5] = page/32, FARG[4:2] = 0. registers.name: PMC_SLPWK_AIPR
registers.title: PMC SleepWalking Activity In Progress Register

fields.name: AIP
fields.text: Shows whether any peripheral is busy; only UARTx and TWIHSx can use SleepWalking.

values.text: No peripheral busy: SleepWalking may be turned on for one or more peripherals and the device may enter Wait mode.
A peripheral is busy: with SleepWalking on for a UARTx or TWIHSx, the device must stay out of Wait mode.

registers.name: PIO_PER
registers.title: PIO Enable Register
notes: Writes are accepted only while PIO_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 gives control of that pin to the PIO.

values.text: The PIO takes control of the pin; the peripheral loses it.

registers.name: PIO_PDR
registers.title: PIO Disable Register
notes: Writes are accepted only while PIO_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 hands that pin back to the peripheral.

values.text: The PIO releases the pin; the peripheral takes control of it.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: reads whether the PIO or the peripheral controls the pin.

values.text: The peripheral controls the line; the PIO is inactive.
The PIO controls the line; the peripheral is inactive.

registers.name: PIO_OER
registers.title: PIO Output Enable Register
notes: Writes are accepted only while PIO_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 turns on that line's output driver.

values.text: The line's output is turned on.

registers.name: PIO_ODR
registers.title: PIO Output Disable Register
notes: Writes are accepted only while PIO_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 turns off that line's output driver.

values.text: The line's output is turned off.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: reads whether the line drives an output.

registers.name: PIO_IFER
registers.title: PIO Input Filter Enable Register
notes: Writes are accepted only while PIO_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 turns on the line's input glitch filter.

values.text: The line's input glitch filter is turned on.

registers.name: PIO_IFDR
registers.title: PIO Input Filter Disable Register
notes: Writes are accepted only while PIO_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 turns off the line's input glitch filter.

values.text: The line's input glitch filter is turned off.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: reads whether the line's input glitch filter is on.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 makes the line's output data 1.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 makes the line's output data 0.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: the data value set to drive on the line.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: the level present on the line.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 turns on the line's input change interrupt.

values.text: The line's input change interrupt is turned on.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 turns off the line's input change interrupt.

values.text: The line's input change interrupt is turned off.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: reads whether the line's input change interrupt is on.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: set when the line's input has changed since reset or since the previous read of PIO_ISR.

values.text: No change seen on the line since the last PIO_ISR read or reset.
One or more changes seen on the line since the last PIO_ISR read or reset.

registers.name: PIO_MDER
registers.title: PIO Multi-driver Enable Register
notes: Writes are accepted only while PIO_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 turns on multi-drive for the line.

values.text: Multi-drive is turned on for the line.

registers.name: PIO_MDDR
registers.title: PIO Multi-driver Disable Register
notes: Writes are accepted only while PIO_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 turns off multi-drive for the line.

values.text: Multi-drive is turned off for the line.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: reads whether multi-drive is on for the line.

values.text: Multi-drive off: the pin is driven both high and low.
Multi-drive on: the pin is driven low only.

registers.name: PIO_PUDR
registers.title: PIO Pull-Up Disable Register
notes: Writes are accepted only while PIO_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: P
fields.text: One bit per I/O line: writing 1 turns off the line's pull-up resistor.

values.text: The line's pull-up is turned off.

values.text: Page-mode asynchronous burst reads on this chip select.

fields.text: Chooses whether the TDF wait states may overlap the next access's setup.

values.text: Off: all TDF wait states pass before the next access starts.
On: the TDF wait states overlap the setup of the next read or write.

fields.name: TDF_CYCLES
fields.text: Clock cycles, 0 to 15, the external device takes to let go of the data bus after the read strobe rises; one more full turnaround cycle always follows, so no other chip select gets the bus for TDF_CYCLES + 1 cycles.

fields.name: DBW
fields.text: Width of the external data bus.

fields.name: BAT
fields.text: How byte accesses are signalled; applies only when DBW selects a 16-bit bus.

values.name: BYTE_SELECT
values.text: Byte select: writes use NCS, NWE, NBS0 and NBS1; reads use NCS, NRD, NBS0 and NBS1.

values.name: BYTE_WRITE
values.text: Byte write: writes use NCS, NWR0 and NWR1; reads use NCS and NRD.

fields.name: EXNW_MODE
fields.text: How the NWAIT input stretches an access; it is sampled only during the read or write strobe pulse, and using it needs a hold of at least one cycle on that strobe.

values.name: DISABLED
values.text: Off: NWAIT is ignored on this chip select.

values.name: FROZEN
values.text: Frozen: while NWAIT is asserted the access stops where it is, and it resumes from that point once NWAIT is deasserted.

values.name: READY
values.text: Ready: NWAIT is checked at the end of the strobe pulse; high lets the access finish, low stretches it until NWAIT goes high.

fields.name: WRITE_MODE
fields.text: Chooses which signal controls a write: NCS or NWE.

values.text: NCS controls the write; with TDF_MODE = 1 the TDF wait states come after the NCS setup.
NWE controls the write; with TDF_MODE = 1 the TDF wait states come after the NWE setup.

fields.name: READ_MODE
fields.text: Chooses which signal controls a read: NCS or NRD.

values.text: NCS controls the read; with TDF cycles set the bus is busy after NCS rises, and with TDF_MODE = 1 the TDF wait states come after the NCS setup.
NRD controls the read; with TDF cycles set the bus is busy after NRD rises, and with TDF_MODE = 1 the TDF wait states come after the NRD setup.

fields.name: ISI_CDC
fields.text: Writing 1 turns on the codec datapath to capture one full-resolution frame; ignored while ISI_SR.CDC_PND is set.

fields.name: ISI_SRST
fields.text: Writing 1 asks for a software reset of the ISI; poll ISI_SR.SRST for completion.

fields.name: ISI_DIS
fields.text: Writing 1 asks to disable the ISI; ignored if ISI_EN is written 1 at the same time; poll ISI_SR.DIS_DONE for completion.

fields.name: ISI_EN

fields.name: FR_OVR
fields.text: Frame rate overrun flag; cleared by reading ISI_SR.

values.text: A VSYNC arrived while FIFOs were being flushed since the last read; the current frame is skipped.

fields.name: CRC_ERR
fields.text: Embedded-synchronization CRC error flag; cleared by reading ISI_SR.

values.text: No CRC error in the SAV/EAV codes.
With CRC_SYNC set, an uncorrected error was found since the last read; the frame is dropped and the ISI waits for the next one.

fields.name: C_OVR
fields.text: Codec path input FIFO overflow flag; cleared by reading ISI_SR.

values.text: Since the last read, a sample was written to the full codec input FIFO.

fields.name: P_OVR

values.text: Since the last read, a sample was written to the full preview input FIFO.

fields.name: SIP

values.text: Synchronizing; channel status must not be changed.

values.text: A preview channel transfer finished since the last read.

fields.name: DIS_DONE
fields.text: Disable finished flag; cleared by reading ISI_SR.

values.text: Disable not finished, if one was asked for.

values.name: PASSWD
values.text: Key ("ISI" in ASCII); any other value cancels the WPEN write. Reads as 0.

fields.name: WPEN
fields.text: Turns write protection on or off, given the right WPKEY.

fields.text: Which register a blocked write went to.

values.text: No violation since the last read.
Blocked write to ISI_CFG1 since the last read.

values.text: No violation since the last read.
A violation happened since the last read; a blocked write to a protected register is named in WPVSRC.

fields.name: TXLPIEN
fields.text: Set to send Low Power Idle (LPI) at once.

fields.name: FNP
fields.text: Write 1 to drop the next packet held in the external RX DPRAM; it acts only while the DMA is not already moving a stored packet from the DPRAM to memory.

fields.name: TXPBPF
fields.text: Sends a PFC priority-based pause frame built from the values held in the Transmit PFC Pause Register.

fields.name: ENPBPR
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on PFC priority-based pause reception, so PFC can be negotiated and priority-based pause frames are recognized.

fields.name: SRTSM
fields.text: Write 1 to have each received frame's CRC overwritten with the 1588 timer nanoseconds value captured as the frame passed the time stamp point; GMAC_NCFGR.RFCS must not be 1 when the timer is to be captured.

values.text: Every received frame's CRC holds a time stamp.

fields.name: TXZQPF
fields.text: Write 1 to send a pause frame with a zero quantum; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXPF
fields.text: Write 1 to send a pause frame; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: THALT
fields.text: Write 1 to stop transmitting once any frame in progress finishes; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TSTART
fields.text: Write 1 to begin transmitting; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: BP
fields.text: In 10M or 100M half duplex, writing 1 forces a collision on every received frame; gigabit half duplex ignores it.

values.text: Collisions forced in 10M and 100M half duplex.

fields.name: WESTAT
fields.text: Write 1 to allow writes to the statistics registers, for functional testing.

fields.name: INCSTAT
fields.text: Write 1 to add one to every statistics register, for testing; writing 0 does nothing. Always reads 0.

fields.name: CLRSTAT
fields.text: Write 1 to zero the statistics registers; writing 0 does nothing. Always reads 0.

fields.name: MPE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the management port on; writing 0 turns it off, leaving MDIO high impedance and driving MDC low impedance.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: Write 1 to let the transmitter send data; writing 0 stops transmission at once, clears the transmit pipeline and control registers, and points the Transmit Queue Pointer back at the first transmit descriptor.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: Write 1 to let the GMAC receive; writing 0 stops reception at once and clears the receive pipeline, leaving the Receive Queue Pointer unchanged.

fields.name: LBL
fields.text: Write 1 to loop GTX to GRX and GTXEN to GRXDV and force full duplex. GRXCK and GTXCK may misbehave while switching in or out of this loop back, so receive and transmit must already be off when switching.

fields.name: IRXER
fields.text: When 1, GRXER has no effect on the GMAC while GRXDV is low. Set it when the RMGII wrapper runs in half duplex.

fields.name: RXBP
fields.text: When 1, frames with a non-standard preamble are kept, not rejected.

fields.name: IPGSEN
fields.text: Write 1 to let the transmit IPG grow past 96 bit times, by the previous frame's length and the IPG Stretch Register.

fields.name: IRXFCS
fields.text: Write 1 to keep frames that have FCS/CRC errors; 0 for normal operation. Bad-FCS frames are still counted in the statistics and their FCS status is put in their DMA descriptor.

fields.name: EFRHD
fields.text: Write 1 to allow receiving frames in half duplex while transmitting.

fields.name: RXCOEN
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the receive checksum engine; any frame whose IP, TCP or UDP checksum is wrong is then dropped.

fields.name: DCPF
fields.text: Write 1 to keep valid pause frames out of memory, whatever CAF, a hash match or a type ID match say; a pause frame matching a destination address is still copied. Received pause frames still count in the pause statistics and still pause transmission.

fields.name: DBW
fields.text: Data bus width; the default is 64 bits.

fields.name: CLK
fields.text: Sets the divider that makes the management data clock (MDC) from MAIN_CLK; choose it by the MAIN_CLK speed so MDC stays at or below 2.5 MHz for 802.3 conformance. MDC runs only during MDIO reads and writes.

fields.name: RFCS
fields.text: Write 1 to store received frames in memory without their last 4 bytes (the FCS); the reported frame length is then four bytes less.

fields.name: LFERD
fields.text: Write 1 to drop frames whose measured length is less than their length field (bytes 13 and 14 of a frame without a VLAN tag); applies only to length fields below 0x0600.

fields.name: RXBUFO
fields.text: Number of bytes the received data is shifted in from the start of the receive buffer.

fields.name: PEN
fields.text: When 1, transmission pauses on receipt of a non-zero 802.3 classic pause frame, provided PFC has not been negotiated.

fields.name: RTY
fields.text: Write 0 for normal operation. When 1, the back-off between collisions is always one slot time, for testing the too-many-retries case; it also makes the pause counter decrement every GRXCK cycle in place of every 512 bit times, for pause frame tests.

fields.name: MAXFS
fields.text: Write 1 to accept frames up to 1536 bytes; when 0, frames longer than 1518 bytes are rejected.

fields.name: UNIHEN
fields.text: Write 1 to accept unicast frames whose destination address 6-bit hash selects a set bit in the Hash Register; 0 turns unicast hashing off.

fields.name: MTIHEN
fields.text: Write 1 to accept multicast frames whose destination address 6-bit hash selects a set bit in the Hash Register; 0 turns multicast hashing off.

fields.name: NBC
fields.text: Write 1 to reject frames sent to the broadcast address 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF; 0 accepts them.

fields.name: CAF
fields.text: Write 1 to accept every valid frame.

fields.name: JFRAME
fields.text: Write 1 to accept jumbo frames of up to 10240 bytes; the default jumbo length is 10240 bytes.

fields.name: DNVLAN
fields.text: Write 1 to pass only VLAN-tagged frames to address matching; 0 passes tagged and untagged frames.

fields.name: FD
fields.text: Write 1 for full duplex: the transmitter ignores collision and carrier sense, and reception goes on while transmitting. 0 turns full duplex off.

fields.name: SPD
fields.text: Write 1 for 100 Mbps, 0 for 10 Mbps.

registers.name: GMAC_NSR
registers.title: GMAC Network Status Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x000001X0.

fields.name: RXLPIS
fields.text: Set while LPI is detected, cleared when normal idle is detected; each change raises an interrupt.

fields.name: IDLE
fields.text: Reads 1 when the PHY management logic is idle, its operation done.

fields.name: MDIO
fields.text: State of the GMDIO pin.

fields.name: RMII
fields.text: Selects RMII or MII.

fields.name: DDRP
fields.text: Chooses what happens to received packets when no AHB resource is free. Writes are ignored unless the DMA runs in full store-and-forward packet buffer mode.

values.text: Packets wait in the SRAM packet buffer until an AHB buffer frees up.
Packets in the receive packet buffer are discarded when no AHB resource is free.

fields.name: DRBS
fields.text: Size of each buffer in AHB system memory that received data is written to, in units of 64 bytes: 0x02 is 128 bytes, 0x18 is 1536 bytes (one maximum-length frame), 0xA0 is 10240 bytes (one 10K jumbo frame). Never write 0x00.

fields.name: TXCOEN
fields.text: Turns on transmit IP, TCP and UDP checksum generation.

values.text: Checksums computed and inserted in transmitted frames.

fields.name: TXPBMS
fields.text: When 0, the transmit packet buffer uses half its memory, so the GMAC uses less; write 1 when the full configured memory is present. Sizes shown are for the default 4 KB maximum.

fields.name: RXBMS
fields.text: Sets the receive packet buffer to the full default size, or a half, quarter or eighth of it.

fields.name: ESPA
fields.text: Endian swap for packet data accesses on AHB.

fields.name: ESMA
fields.text: Endian swap for management descriptor accesses on AHB.

fields.name: FBLDO
fields.text: AHB burst length tried when moving frame data, where space and data size permit; otherwise SINGLE transfers are used. Not used for DMA management operations. Writes are forced to one-hot by priority (x = don't care).

fields.name: HRESP
fields.text: Set when the DMA sees an HRESP not OK. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: TXCOMP
fields.text: Set when a frame has gone out. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: TFC
fields.text: Set on an error while reading a transmit frame from AHB: an HRESP error, or buffers running out mid frame (transmission then stops, the FCS is bad and GTXER is asserted). In DMA packet buffer mode also set when one frame is too big for the configured packet buffer. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: TXGO
fields.text: Reads 1 while transmission is active; with the DMA interface it is the TXGO variable of the transmit buffer description.

fields.name: RLE
fields.text: Retry limit exceeded. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: COL
fields.text: In 10 or 100 Mbps mode, set on a collision or a late collision; in gigabit mode, set on a collision but not a late collision. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: UBR
fields.text: Set on reading a transmit buffer descriptor whose used bit is 1. Write 1 to clear.

registers.name: GMAC_RBQB
registers.title: GMAC Receive Buffer Queue Base Address Register

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Start address of the receive buffer queue.

registers.name: GMAC_TBQB
registers.title: GMAC Transmit Buffer Queue Base Address Register

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Start address of the transmit buffer queue.

fields.name: HNO
fields.text: Set when the DMA sees an HRESP not OK. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: RXOVR
fields.text: Set when the RX FIFO overflows and cannot hold a received frame, when a frame's receive status was not collected as it ended, or when the packet buffer overflows; the buffer is recovered after an overrun. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: REC
fields.text: Set once at least one frame has arrived and been stored in memory. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: BNA
fields.text: Set when the DMA went to fetch a new buffer and found its pointer owned by the processor; the DMA re-reads the pointer at each end of frame until it finds a valid one. Set again after each failed descriptor read, even if software cleared it meanwhile. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: TSUTIMCMP
fields.text: Set when the TSU timer count equals the programmed value. Cleared on read.

fields.name: WOL
fields.text: Set when a Wake on LAN message has been received.

fields.name: RXLPISBC
fields.text: Set when the receive LPI indication status bit changes. Cleared on read.

fields.name: SRI
fields.text: Set when the TSU seconds register has incremented. Cleared on read.

fields.name: PDRSFT
fields.text: Set when a PTP pdelay_resp frame has gone out. Cleared on read.

fields.name: PDRQFT
fields.text: Set when a PTP pdelay_req frame has gone out. Cleared on read.

fields.name: PDRSFR
fields.text: Set when a PTP pdelay_resp frame has arrived. Cleared on read.

fields.name: PDRQFR
fields.text: Set when a PTP pdelay_req frame has arrived. Cleared on read.

fields.name: SFT
fields.text: Set when a PTP sync frame has gone out. Cleared on read.

fields.name: DRQFT
fields.text: Set when a PTP delay_req frame has gone out. Cleared on read.

fields.name: SFR
fields.text: Set when a PTP sync frame has arrived. Cleared on read.

fields.name: DRQFR
fields.text: Set when a PTP delay_req frame has arrived. Cleared on read.

fields.name: PFTR
fields.text: Set when a pause frame started from the Network Control Register has been sent. Cleared on read.

fields.name: PTZ
fields.text: Set when the Pause Time Register (0x38) reaches zero, or on receipt of a valid pause frame whose pause quantum is zero. Cleared on read.

fields.name: PFNZ
fields.text: Set when a valid pause frame arrives with a non-zero pause quantum. Cleared on read.

fields.name: HRESP
fields.text: Set when the DMA sees an HRESP not OK. Cleared on read.

fields.name: ROVR
fields.text: Follows the receive overrun status bit: set when it sets. Cleared on read.

fields.name: TCOMP
fields.text: Set when a frame has gone out. Cleared on read.

fields.name: TFC
fields.text: Set on an error while reading a transmit frame from AHB, HRESP errors and buffers running out mid frame among them.

fields.name: RLEX
fields.text: Set on a transmit error from too many retries or from a late collision; a late collision sets it only in gigabit mode, where no retry is made. Cleared on read.

fields.name: TUR
fields.text: Set when the transmitter had to end a frame early because no more data came; when a transmit status write back was attempted before the previous one finished; or when the transmit DMA had put the SOP data in the FIFO and then the AHB was not granted in time, an AHB not OK response came back, or the used bit was read.

fields.name: TXUBR
fields.text: Set on reading a transmit buffer descriptor whose used bit is 1. Cleared on read.

fields.name: RXUBR
fields.text: Set on reading a receive buffer descriptor whose used bit is 1. Cleared on read.

fields.name: RCOMP
fields.text: Set when a frame has been stored in memory. Cleared on read.

fields.name: MFS
fields.text: Set when the PHY Maintenance Register has finished its operation. Cleared on read.

fields.name: CLTTO
fields.text: Chooses a clause 22 or clause 45 frame.

fields.name: OP

fields.name: PHYA
fields.text: PHY address.

fields.name: REGA
fields.text: Which PHY register is accessed.

fields.name: WTN
fields.text: Write ten: always write 0b10.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: For a write, the data sent to the PHY; after a read, the data returned by the PHY.

fields.name: RPQ
fields.text: Present value of the received pause quantum, counted down every 512 bit times.

fields.name: TPQ
fields.text: Pause quantum put in transmitted pause frames.

registers.name: GMAC_TPSF
registers.title: GMAC TX Partial Store and Forward Register

fields.name: ENTXP
fields.text: Enable TX partial store and forward operation.

fields.name: TPB1ADR
fields.text: Watermark for transmit partial store and forward.

registers.name: GMAC_RPSF
registers.title: GMAC RX Partial Store and Forward Register

fields.name: ENRXP
fields.text: Enable RX partial store and forward operation.

fields.name: RPB1ADR
fields.text: Watermark for receive partial store and forward; resets to 1.

registers.name: GMAC_RJFML
registers.title: GMAC RX Jumbo Frame Max Length Register

fields.name: FML
fields.text: Largest length of a received jumbo frame.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Bits 31:0 of the 64-bit hash address.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Bits 63:32 of the 64-bit hash address.

registers.name: GMAC_SABx
registers.title: GMAC Specific Address n Bottom Register

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Bits 31:0 of the destination address. Bit 0 marks multicast or unicast and is the least significant bit of the first byte received.

registers.name: GMAC_SATx
registers.title: GMAC Specific Address n Top Register

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Bits 47:32 of the destination address.

registers.name: GMAC_TIDMx
registers.title: GMAC Type ID Match n Register

fields.name: ENIDn
fields.text: Enable copying of frames matching type ID n.

values.text: TID n left out of the match.
TID n included in the match.

fields.name: TID
fields.text: Type ID n, compared with the type ID/length field of received frames.

fields.name: MTI
fields.text: Wake on a multicast hash match.

fields.name: SA1
fields.text: Wake on a Specific Address Register 1 match.

fields.name: ARP
fields.text: Wake on an ARP request.

fields.name: MAG
fields.text: Wake on a magic packet.

fields.name: IP
fields.text: Low 16 bits of the target IP address an ARP request must match to raise a Wake on LAN event; 0x0001 to 0xFFFF raise the event on a match.

values.text: No event, even on a match.

fields.name: FL
fields.text: IPG stretch: FL[7:0] times the previous frame's length (preamble included), divided by FL[15:8]+1 (the +1 avoids a divide by zero). When the result is above 96 and GMAC_NCFGR.IPGSEN is 1, it becomes the transmit inter-packet gap.

fields.name: ESVLAN
fields.text: Turns stacked VLAN processing on.

fields.name: VLAN_TYPE
fields.text: With ESVLAN=1, a received frame's first VLAN tag is accepted only if its type field equals this value or the standard 0x8100. The second tag of a stacked VLAN frame matches only if its type is 0x8100.

fields.name: PQ
fields.text: With GMAC_NCFGR.RFCS at 1: for each bit at 0 the matching PFC pause frame quantum comes from GMAC_TPQ; for each bit at 1 that quantum is zero.

fields.name: PEV
fields.text: With GMAC_NCFGR.RFCS at 1, the priority enable vector sent in PFC priority-based pause frames.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: A 1 masks the matching bit of GMAC_SAB1.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: A 1 masks the matching bit of GMAC_SAT1.

fields.name: NANOSEC
fields.text: Compared with TSU timer bits 45:24, the upper 22 bits of the nanoseconds value.

registers.name: GMAC_SCL
registers.title: GMAC 1588 Timer Second Comparison Low Register

fields.name: SEC
fields.text: Compared with bits 31:0 of the TSU timer seconds value.

registers.name: GMAC_SCH
registers.title: GMAC 1588 Timer Second Comparison High Register

fields.name: SEC
fields.text: Compared with bits 47:32 of the TSU timer seconds value.

registers.name: GMAC_EFTSH
registers.title: GMAC PTP Event Frame Transmitted Seconds High Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer seconds (upper bits) when a PTP transmit primary event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_EFRSH
registers.title: GMAC PTP Event Frame Received Seconds High Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer seconds (upper bits) when a PTP transmit primary event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_PEFTSH
registers.title: GMAC PTP Peer Event Frame Transmitted Seconds High Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer seconds (upper bits) when a PTP transmit peer event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_PEFRSH
registers.title: GMAC PTP Peer Event Frame Received Seconds High Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer seconds (upper bits) when a PTP transmit peer event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

fields.name: TXO
fields.text: Bits 31:0 of the 48-bit count of octets sent in error-free frames of any type, read over two registers; octets of automatically generated pause frames are left out.

fields.name: TXO
fields.text: Bits 47:32 of the 48-bit count of octets sent in error-free frames of any type, read over two registers; octets of automatically generated pause frames are left out.

fields.name: FTX
fields.text: Count of frames sent without error (with no underrun and not too many retries), pause frames left out.

fields.name: BFTX
fields.text: Count of broadcast frames sent without error (with no underrun and not too many retries), pause frames left out.

fields.name: MFTX
fields.text: Count of multicast frames sent without error (with no underrun and not too many retries), pause frames left out.

fields.name: PFTX
fields.text: Count of pause frames sent. Only those started from the register interface or the external pause pins count here; pause frames coming through the FIFO interface count as transmitted frames.

fields.name: NFTX
fields.text: Count of 64-byte frames sent without error (with no underrun and not too many retries), pause frames left out.

registers.name: GMAC_TBFT127
registers.title: GMAC 65 to 127 Byte Frames Transmitted Register

fields.name: NFTX
fields.text: Count of 65 to 127 byte frames sent without error (with no underrun and not too many retries), pause frames left out.

registers.name: GMAC_TBFT255
registers.title: GMAC 128 to 255 Byte Frames Transmitted Register

fields.name: NFTX
fields.text: Count of 128 to 255 byte frames sent without error (with no underrun and not too many retries).

registers.name: GMAC_TBFT511
registers.title: GMAC 256 to 511 Byte Frames Transmitted Register

fields.name: NFTX
fields.text: Count of 256 to 511 byte frames sent without error (with no underrun and not too many retries).

registers.name: GMAC_TBFT1023
registers.title: GMAC 512 to 1023 Byte Frames Transmitted Register

fields.name: NFTX
fields.text: Count of 512 to 1023 byte frames sent without error (with no underrun and not too many retries).

registers.name: GMAC_TBFT1518
registers.title: GMAC 1024 to 1518 Byte Frames Transmitted Register

fields.name: NFTX
fields.text: Count of 1024 to 1518 byte frames sent without error (with no underrun and not too many retries).

registers.name: GMAC_GTBFT1518
registers.title: GMAC Greater Than 1518 Byte Frames Transmitted Register

fields.name: NFTX
fields.text: Count of frames of 1518 bytes or more sent without error (with no underrun and not too many retries).

fields.name: TXUNR
fields.text: Count of frames not sent because of a transmit underrun; when it counts, no other statistics register does.

fields.name: SCOL
fields.text: Count of frames that met exactly one collision before being sent with no underrun.

fields.name: MCOL
fields.text: Count of frames that met two to fifteen collisions before being sent with no underrun and not too many retries.

fields.name: XCOL
fields.text: Count of frames not sent after meeting 16 collisions.

fields.name: LCOL
fields.text: Count of collisions after the 512-bit slot time. In 10/100 mode each one is counted twice, as a collision and as a late collision; in gigabit mode it aborts the frame, so the single and multiple collision counts are not updated.

fields.name: DEFT
fields.text: Count of frames deferred on their first transmit attempt because carrier sense was active; frames that met a collision or a transmit underrun are not counted.

fields.name: CSR
fields.text: Count of frames sent with no underrun where carrier sense was never seen, or dropped after being asserted, in a collision-free frame. Counts only in half duplex. A carrier sense error does nothing but add to this count; the other statistics registers are unaffected.

fields.name: RXO
fields.text: Bits 31:0 of the 48-bit count of octets received in error-free frames of any type, read over two registers; pause frame octets are left out, counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

fields.name: RXO
fields.text: Bits 47:32 of the 48-bit count of octets received in error-free frames of any type, read over two registers; pause frame octets are left out, counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

fields.name: FRX
fields.text: Count of frames received without error, pause frames left out; counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

fields.name: BFRX
fields.text: Count of broadcast frames received without error, pause frames left out; counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

fields.name: MFRX
fields.text: Count of multicast frames received without error, pause frames left out; counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

fields.name: PFRX
fields.text: Count of pause frames received without error.

fields.name: NFRX
fields.text: Count of 64-byte frames received without error, pause frames left out; counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

registers.name: GMAC_TBFR127
registers.title: GMAC 65 to 127 Byte Frames Received Register

fields.name: NFRX
fields.text: Count of 65 to 127 byte frames received without error, pause frames left out; counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

registers.name: GMAC_TBFR255
registers.title: GMAC 128 to 255 Byte Frames Received Register

fields.name: NFRX
fields.text: Count of 128 to 255 byte frames received without error, pause frames left out; counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

registers.name: GMAC_TBFR511
registers.title: GMAC 256 to 511 Byte Frames Received Register

fields.name: NFRX
fields.text: Count of 256 to 511 byte frames received without error, pause frames left out; counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

registers.name: GMAC_TBFR1023
registers.title: GMAC 512 to 1023 Byte Frames Received Register

fields.name: NFRX
fields.text: Count of 512 to 1023 byte frames received without error, pause frames left out; counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

registers.name: GMAC_TBFR1518
registers.title: GMAC 1024 to 1518 Byte Frames Received Register

fields.name: NFRX
fields.text: Count of 1024 to 1518 byte frames received without error, with no underrun and not too many retries.

registers.name: GMAC_TMXBFR
registers.title: GMAC 1519 to Maximum Byte Frames Received Register

fields.name: NFRX
fields.text: Count of frames of 1519 bytes up to the maximum received without error; the maximum is set by GMAC_NCFGR.MAXFS (1536 bytes) or GMAC_NCFGR.JFRAME (10240 bytes). Pause frames left out; counted only when the frame passes the filter and is copied to memory.

fields.name: UFRX
fields.text: Count of received frames shorter than 64 bytes (10/100 or gigabit full duplex) with no CRC or alignment error. In gigabit half duplex, counts frames short of the 512-byte minimum slot time, or, once bursting is on, short of the minimum frame size.

fields.name: OFRX
fields.text: Count of received frames longer than 1518 bytes (1536 if GMAC_NCFGR.MAXFS is 1, 10240 if GMAC_NCFGR.JFRAME is 1) that have no CRC, alignment or receive symbol error.

fields.name: JRX
fields.text: Count of received frames longer than 1518 bytes (1536 if GMAC_NCFGR.MAXFS is 1, 10240 if GMAC_NCFGR.JFRAME is 1) that have a CRC, alignment or receive symbol error.

registers.name: GMAC_FCSE
registers.title: GMAC Frame Check Sequence Errors Register

fields.name: FCKR
fields.text: Count of frames a whole number of bytes long, with bad CRC, from 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 if GMAC_NCFGR.MAXFS is 1, 10240 if GMAC_NCFGR.JFRAME is 1). Also counts a symbol error in a frame of valid length and whole bytes. A bad-FCS frame counts even when it is copied to memory under ignore-FCS mode (GMAC_NCFGR.IRXFCS=1).

registers.name: GMAC_LFFE
registers.title: GMAC Length Field Frame Errors Register

fields.name: LFER
fields.text: Count of received frames whose measured length is less than their length field (bytes 13 and 14). Counted only when the length field is below 0x0600, the frame is not too long, and GMAC_NCFGR.LFERD is 1.

fields.name: RXSE
fields.text: Count of frames with GRXER asserted during reception. In 10/100 mode counted whatever the frame length; in gigabit mode the frame must meet the slot time, and in gigabit half duplex carrier extension errors count too. A symbol error in a frame of 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 if GMAC_NCFGR.MAXFS is 1, 10240 if GMAC_NCFGR.JFRAME is 1) also counts as an FCS or alignment error; a longer frame counts as a jabber.

fields.name: AER
fields.text: Count of frames not a whole number of bytes long whose CRC is bad once cut to whole bytes, from 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 if GMAC_NCFGR.MAXFS is 1, 10240 if GMAC_NCFGR.JFRAME is 1). Also counts a symbol error in a frame of valid length that is not whole bytes.

fields.name: RXRER
fields.text: Receive resource errors: counts frames not a whole number of bytes long with bad CRC once cut to whole bytes, from 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 if GMAC_NCFGR.MAXFS is 1, 10240 if GMAC_NCFGR.JFRAME is 1), plus symbol errors in such frames of valid length.

fields.name: RXOVR
fields.text: Count of address-matched frames not copied to memory because of a receive overrun.

registers.name: GMAC_IHCE
registers.title: GMAC IP Header Checksum Errors Register

fields.name: HCKER
fields.text: Count of frames dropped for a bad IP header checksum that are 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 if GMAC_NCFGR.MAXFS is 1, 10240 if GMAC_NCFGR.JFRAME is 1) and have no CRC, alignment or symbol error.

fields.name: TCKER
fields.text: Count of frames dropped for a bad TCP checksum that are 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 if GMAC_NCFGR.MAXFS is 1, 10240 if GMAC_NCFGR.JFRAME is 1) and have no CRC, alignment or symbol error.

fields.name: UCKER
fields.text: Count of frames dropped for a bad UDP checksum that are 64 to 1518 bytes (1536 if GMAC_NCFGR.MAXFS is 1, 10240 if GMAC_NCFGR.JFRAME is 1) and have no CRC, alignment or symbol error.

fields.name: LSBTIR
fields.text: Low 16 bits of the 24-bit timer increment: the sub-nanosecond amount added to the 1588 timer each clock cycle. Bit n is worth 2^(n-16) ns, a resolution of about 15.2E-15 s.

fields.name: TCS
fields.text: Writable seconds count of the IEEE 1588 timer (upper bits); it goes up by 1 each time the nanoseconds counter reaches one second, and may also step when the Timer Adjust Register is written.

fields.name: TCS
fields.text: Writable seconds count of the IEEE 1588 timer (lower 32 bits); it goes up by 1 each time the nanoseconds counter reaches one second, and may also step when the Timer Adjust Register is written.

fields.name: TNS
fields.text: Writable nanoseconds count of the IEEE 1588 timer; it grows by the Timer Increment Register value each clock cycle and can be changed through the Timer Adjust Register.

fields.name: ADJ
fields.text: Direction of the adjustment: 1 subtracts from the 1588 timer, 0 adds to it.

fields.name: ITDT
fields.text: Nanoseconds added to or taken from the 1588 timer nanoseconds register; the seconds register steps up or down when needed.

fields.name: NIT
fields.text: How many increments pass before the alternative increment is applied.

fields.name: ACNS
fields.text: Alternative number of nanoseconds added to the 1588 timer nanoseconds register each clock cycle.

fields.name: CNS
fields.text: Number of nanoseconds added to the 1588 timer nanoseconds register each clock cycle.

registers.name: GMAC_EFTSL
registers.title: GMAC PTP Event Frame Transmitted Seconds Low Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer seconds when a PTP transmit primary event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_EFTN
registers.title: GMAC PTP Event Frame Transmitted Nanoseconds Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer nanoseconds when a PTP transmit primary event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_EFRSL
registers.title: GMAC PTP Event Frame Received Seconds Low Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer seconds when a PTP receive primary event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_EFRN
registers.title: GMAC PTP Event Frame Received Nanoseconds Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer nanoseconds when a PTP receive primary event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_PEFTSL
registers.title: GMAC PTP Peer Event Frame Transmitted Seconds Low Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer seconds when a PTP transmit peer event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_PEFTN
registers.title: GMAC PTP Peer Event Frame Transmitted Nanoseconds Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer nanoseconds when a PTP transmit peer event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_PEFRSL
registers.title: GMAC PTP Peer Event Frame Received Seconds Low Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer seconds when a PTP receive peer event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_PEFRN
registers.title: GMAC PTP Peer Event Frame Received Nanoseconds Register

fields.name: RUD
fields.text: Captures the IEEE 1588 timer nanoseconds when a PTP receive peer event frame's SFD passes the MII; each capture raises an interrupt.

fields.name: COUNT
fields.text: Count of changes from normal idle to low power idle on receive. Cleared on read.

fields.name: LPITIME
fields.text: Goes up once every 16 MCK cycles while GMAC_NSR.RXLPIS is set. Cleared on read.

fields.name: COUNT
fields.text: Count of rising edges of GMAC_NCR.TXLPIEN. Cleared on read.

fields.name: LPITIME
fields.text: Goes up once every 16 MCK cycles while GMAC_NCR.TXLPIEN is set. Cleared on read.

registers.name: GMAC_ISRPQx
registers.title: GMAC Interrupt Status Register Priority Queue x

fields.name: HRESP
fields.text: Interrupt status for this priority queue: HRESP not OK.

fields.name: ROVR
fields.text: Interrupt status for this priority queue: receive overrun.

fields.name: TCOMP
fields.text: Interrupt status for this priority queue: transmit complete.

fields.name: TFC
fields.text: Set on an error part way through reading a transmit frame from AHB, HRESP errors and buffers running out mid frame among them.

fields.name: RLEX
fields.text: Interrupt status for this priority queue: retry limit exceeded or late collision.

fields.name: RXUBR
fields.text: Interrupt status for this priority queue: RX used bit read.

fields.name: RCOMP
fields.text: Interrupt status for this priority queue: receive complete.

registers.name: GMAC_TBQBAPQx
registers.title: GMAC Transmit Buffer Queue Base Address Register Priority Queue x

fields.name: TXBQBA
fields.text: Start address of this priority queue's transmit buffer queue.

registers.name: GMAC_RBQBAPQx
registers.title: GMAC Receive Buffer Queue Base Address Register Priority Queue x

fields.name: RXBQBA
fields.text: Start address of this priority queue's receive buffer queue.

registers.name: GMAC_RBSRPQx
registers.title: GMAC Receive Buffer Size Register Priority Queue x

fields.name: RBS
fields.text: Size of each receive buffer in AHB system memory for this queue, in units of 64 bytes: 0x01 is 64 bytes, 0x02 is 128, 0x18 is 1536 (one maximum-length frame), 0xA0 is 10240 (one 10K jumbo frame). Never write 0.

fields.name: QAE
fields.text: Credit-based shaping on queue A, the second highest priority queue.

fields.name: QBE
fields.text: Credit-based shaping on queue B, the highest priority queue.

registers.name: GMAC_CBSISQA
registers.title: GMAC Credit-Based Shaping IdleSlope Register for Queue A

fields.name: IS
fields.text: Queue A IdleSlope, in bytes per second: the rate credit builds while a packet waits to go. It must not exceed the port transmit rate set by the link speed, e.g. 100 Mb/s = 0x017D7840; giving a queue half the bandwidth at 100 Mb/s means 0x017D7840 / 2.

registers.name: GMAC_CBSISQB
registers.title: GMAC Credit-Based Shaping IdleSlope Register for Queue B

fields.name: IS
fields.text: IdleSlope for queue B in bytes per second: the rate credit builds while a packet waits to go. It must not exceed the port transmit rate set by the link speed, e.g. 100 Mb/s = 0x017D7840; giving a queue half the bandwidth at 100 Mb/s means 0x017D7840 / 2.

registers.name: GMAC_ST1RPQx
registers.title: GMAC Screening Type 1 Register x Priority Queue

fields.name: UDPE
fields.text: Write 1 to match the destination port of received UDP frames against UDPM.

fields.name: DSTCE
fields.text: Write 1 to match the IPv4 DS field or IPv6 TC field of received frames against DSTCM.

fields.name: UDPM
fields.text: UDP destination port compared with received UDP frames when the UDP port match enable is set.

fields.name: DSTCM
fields.text: Value compared with the IPv4 DS field or IPv6 TC field when DSTCE is set.

fields.name: QNB
fields.text: Queue given to a frame that matches.

registers.name: GMAC_ST2RPQx
registers.title: GMAC Screening Type 2 Register x Priority Queue

fields.name: COMPCE
fields.text: Turns compare C on.

values.text: Compare C on, through the register pair COMPC picks.

fields.name: COMPC
fields.text: Selects which GMAC_ST2CW0x/GMAC_ST2CW1x pair is used for compare C. With COMPCE=1 the compare is true when the frame data at the offset ANDed with MASKVAL equals COMPVAL ANDed with MASKVAL.

fields.name: COMPBE
fields.text: Turns compare B on.

values.text: Compare B on, through the register pair COMPB picks.

fields.name: COMPB
fields.text: Selects which GMAC_ST2CW0x/GMAC_ST2CW1x pair is used for compare B. With COMPBE=1 the compare is true when the frame data at the offset ANDed with MASKVAL equals COMPVAL ANDed with MASKVAL.

fields.name: COMPAE
fields.text: Turns compare A on.

values.text: Compare A on, through the register pair COMPA picks.

fields.name: COMPA
fields.text: Selects which GMAC_ST2CW0x/GMAC_ST2CW1x pair is used for compare A. With COMPAE=1 the compare is true when the frame data at the offset ANDed with MASKVAL equals COMPVAL ANDed with MASKVAL.

fields.name: ETHE
fields.text: Turns EtherType matching on.

values.text: EtherType matched against bits 15:0 of the register chosen by I2ETH.

fields.name: I2ETH
fields.text: With ETHE=1, picks the register whose bits 15:0 are compared with the frame's EtherType (the last one in the header of a VLAN-tagged frame).

fields.name: VLANE
fields.text: Turns VLAN priority matching on.

fields.name: VLANP
fields.text: With VLANE=1, value compared with the VLAN priority field of received frames.

fields.name: QNB
fields.text: Queue given to a frame that matches.

registers.name: GMAC_IERPQx
registers.title: GMAC Interrupt Enable Register Priority Queue x

fields.name: HRESP
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the HRESP not OK interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: ROVR
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the receive overrun interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: TCOMP
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the transmit complete interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: TFC
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the transmit frame corruption (AHB error) interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: RLEX
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the retry limit exceeded or late collision interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: RXUBR
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the RX used bit read interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: RCOMP
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the receive complete interrupt; 0 has no effect.

registers.name: GMAC_IDRPQx
registers.title: GMAC Interrupt Disable Register Priority Queue x

fields.name: HRESP
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the HRESP not OK interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: ROVR
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the receive overrun interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: TCOMP
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the transmit complete interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: TFC
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the transmit frame corruption (AHB error) interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: RLEX
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the retry limit exceeded or late collision interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: RXUBR
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the RX used bit read interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: RCOMP
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the receive complete interrupt; 0 has no effect.

registers.name: GMAC_IMRPQx
registers.title: GMAC Interrupt Mask Register Priority Queue x

fields.name: HRESP
fields.text: Mask of the HRESP not OK interrupt: reads 0 when enabled, 1 when disabled. A write sets or clears the matching interrupt status bit, and writing 1 raises the interrupt.

fields.name: ROVR
fields.text: Mask of the receive overrun interrupt: reads 0 when enabled, 1 when disabled. A write sets or clears the matching interrupt status bit, and writing 1 raises the interrupt.

fields.name: TCOMP
fields.text: Mask of the transmit complete interrupt: reads 0 when enabled, 1 when disabled. A write sets or clears the matching interrupt status bit, and writing 1 raises the interrupt.

fields.name: AHB
fields.text: Mask of the AHB error interrupt: reads 0 when enabled, 1 when disabled. A write sets or clears the matching interrupt status bit, and writing 1 raises the interrupt.

fields.name: RLEX
fields.text: Mask of the retry limit exceeded or late collision interrupt: reads 0 when enabled, 1 when disabled. A write sets or clears the matching interrupt status bit, and writing 1 raises the interrupt.

fields.name: RXUBR
fields.text: Mask of the RX used bit read interrupt: reads 0 when enabled, 1 when disabled. A write sets or clears the matching interrupt status bit, and writing 1 raises the interrupt.

fields.name: RCOMP
fields.text: Mask of the receive complete interrupt: reads 0 when enabled, 1 when disabled. A write sets or clears the matching interrupt status bit, and writing 1 raises the interrupt.

registers.name: GMAC_ST2ERx
registers.title: GMAC Screening Type 2 EtherType Register x

fields.name: COMPVAL
fields.text: EtherType value; with GMAC_ST2RPQ.ETHE at 1, the frame's EtherType (the last one in the header of a VLAN-tagged frame) is compared with bits 15:0 of the register chosen by GMAC_ST2RPQ.I2ETH.

registers.name: GMAC_ST2CW0x
registers.title: GMAC Screening Type 2 Compare Word 0 Register x

fields.name: COMPVAL
fields.text: Compare bytes: bits 23:16 are compared with the first and bits 31:24 with the second of the 2 bytes taken from the frame.

fields.name: MASKVAL
fields.text: Mask: the 2 frame bytes ANDed with MASKVAL are compared with COMPVAL ANDed with MASKVAL.

registers.name: GMAC_ST2CW1x
registers.title: GMAC Screening Type 2 Compare Word 1 Register x

fields.name: OFFSSTRT
fields.text: Where the compare offset is counted from.

fields.name: OFFSVAL
fields.text: Offset of the compared bytes, 0 to 127, from the start chosen by OFFSSTRT: the frame start, the byte after the EtherType (the last one in a VLAN-tagged header), after the IPv4 or IPv6 header, or after the TCP/UDP header.

fields.name: UIMOD
fields.text: Selects the role: 0 (HOST) runs the module as a USB host, 1 (DEVICE) as a USB device. Can be written even while USBE = 0 or FRZCLK = 1; clearing USBE leaves it unchanged.

fields.name: UID
fields.text: UID pin enable; keep at 0.

fields.name: USBE
fields.text: Turns the USBHS on. Writing 0 resets the USBHS, shuts off its transceiver and its clock inputs, and resets the registers, which become read-only unless stated otherwise. Can be written even while FRZCLK = 1.

fields.name: FRZCLK
fields.text: Stops the USB clock inputs. Can be written even while USBE = 0; clearing USBE keeps this bit, but the clocks stop whatever it holds.

values.text: Clock inputs stopped, resume detection still working; saves power. Registers become read-only unless stated otherwise.

fields.name: VBUSHWC
fields.text: VBUS hardware control; keep at 1.

values.text: Hardware drives the VBOF pin and resets it on a VBUS problem.
Hardware does not drive the VBOF pin.
Hardware drives the PIO line and resets that pin on a VBUS problem.
Hardware does not drive the PIO line.

fields.name: RDERRE
fields.text: Enables the interrupt raised by USBHS_SR.RDERRI.

registers.name: USBHS_SR
registers.title: General Status Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000400.

fields.name: CLKUSABLE
fields.text: Shows whether the 30 MHz UTMI clock can be used.

fields.name: SPEED
fields.text: Speed of the attached device, set from the mode it runs in.

fields.name: RDERRI
fields.text: Flags an error while a remote device was connecting (host mode only).

values.text: A remote device connection failed; raises a USB interrupt if USBHS_CTRL.RDERRE = 1.

registers.name: USBHS_SCR
registers.title: General Status Clear Register
notes: Reads as 0.

fields.name: RDERRIC
fields.text: Write 1 to clear USBHS_SR.RDERRI.

registers.name: USBHS_SFR
registers.title: General Status Set Register
notes: Reads as 0.

fields.name: VBUSRQS
fields.text: VBUS request set; keep at 1.

fields.name: RDERRIS
fields.text: Write 1 to set USBHS_SR.RDERRI.

values.text: Sets USBHS_SR.RDERRI, for testing or debugging.

fields.name: OPMODE2
fields.text: Puts the UTMI transceiver into a test mode with bit stuffing and NRZI encoding turned off.

values.text: Transceiver test mode with bit stuffing and NRZI encoding off.

fields.name: TSTPCKT
fields.text: Makes the UTMI transceiver send test packets.

fields.name: TSTK
fields.text: Makes the UTMI transceiver drive a high-speed K state.

values.text: Transceiver drives a high-speed K state, for testing.

fields.name: TSTJ
fields.text: Makes the UTMI transceiver drive a high-speed J state.

values.text: Transceiver drives a high-speed J state, for testing.

fields.name: LS
fields.text: Forces low-speed operation. Can be written even while USBHS_CTRL.USBE = 0 or USBHS_CTRL.FRZCLK = 1; clearing USBE leaves it unchanged.

fields.name: SPDCONF
fields.text: Sets the speed the device side works at.

values.name: NORMAL
values.text: Starts at full speed and moves to high speed through a high-speed reset when the other side supports it.

values.name: LOW_POWER
values.text: Low power: for use when high speed is not needed.

values.name: FORCED_FS
values.text: Stays at full speed whatever the host supports.

fields.name: RMWKUP
fields.text: Write 1 to have an upstream resume go out to the host. Hardware clears it after a USB reset or once the resume is out.

values.text: Sends an upstream resume (remote wakeup) to the host.

fields.name: DETACH
fields.text: Disconnects the device from the bus. In high-speed mode, follow a detach with USBHS_CTRL.USBE = 0; to attach again set USBE to 1, then write 0 here.

values.text: Detaches the device: the internal pull-up on D+ and D- is disconnected.

fields.name: ADDEN
fields.text: Makes the address in UADD take effect. A USB reset clears it.

values.text: UADD is used as the USB address.

fields.name: UADD
fields.text: The device's USB address. A USB reset clears it.

fields.name: DMA_7
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 7.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS7 source is cleared.
DMA channel 7 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.DMA_7 = 1.

fields.name: DMA_6
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 6.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS6 source is cleared.
DMA channel 6 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.DMA_6 = 1.

fields.name: DMA_5
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 5.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS5 source is cleared.
DMA channel 5 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.DMA_5 = 1.

fields.name: DMA_4
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 4.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS4 source is cleared.
DMA channel 4 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.DMA_4 = 1.

fields.name: DMA_3
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 3.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS3 source is cleared.
DMA channel 3 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.DMA_3 = 1.

fields.name: DMA_2
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 2.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS2 source is cleared.
DMA channel 2 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.DMA_2 = 1.

fields.name: DMA_1
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 1.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS1 source is cleared.
DMA channel 1 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.DMA_1 = 1.

fields.name: PEP_
fields.text: Interrupt flag of endpoint x, one bit per endpoint.

values.text: Clears once the source is handled.
Endpoint x raised an interrupt (USBHS_DEVEPTISRx, USBHS_DEVEPTIMRx); a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.PEP_x = 1.

fields.name: UPRSM
fields.text: Flags that an upstream resume was sent.

values.text: Cleared by writing 1 to USBHS_DEVICR.UPRSMC, with the USB clock inputs already running.
The USBHS sent an upstream resume; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.UPRSME = 1.

fields.name: EORSM
fields.text: Flags that the host's end of resume was seen.

values.text: A valid end of resume from the host was seen; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.EORSME = 1.

fields.name: WAKEUP
fields.text: Flags a wakeup from bus activity; raised even with the clock frozen by USBHS_CTRL.FRZCLK.

values.text: Cleared by writing 1 to USBHS_DEVICR.WAKEUPC (USB clock inputs already running), or when SUSP sets.
A filtered non-idle signal on the lines woke the USBHS (an upstream resume does not); an interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.WAKEUPE = 1.

fields.name: EORST
fields.text: Flags the end of a USB reset.

values.text: A USB end of reset was seen; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.EORSTE = 1.

fields.name: SOF
fields.text: Flags a received start of frame.

values.text: A SOF PID arrived (every 1 ms); a USB interrupt follows if SOFE = 1. FNUM updates; at high speed MFNUM clears.

fields.name: MSOF
fields.text: Flags a received micro start of frame (high speed).

values.text: At high speed, a micro SOF PID arrived (every 125 μs); a USB interrupt follows if MSOFE = 1. MFNUM updates, FNUM does not.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Flags a suspend state on the bus.

values.text: Cleared by writing 1 to USBHS_DEVICR.SUSPC, or when WAKEUP sets.
The bus sat idle in J state for 3 frames (3 ms), a suspend; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_DEVIMR.SUSPE = 1.

fields.name: EPRST
fields.text: Resets endpoint x, one bit per endpoint. The FIFO counter, reception and transmission start over, but USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.DTSEQ is kept (clear it with USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.RSTDTS, which sets USBHS_DEVEPTIMRx.RSTDT). The endpoint stays configured and enabled. A USB reset clears the bit.

values.text: Ends the reset; the FIFO can be used.

Resets the endpoint x FIFO before anything else, after a hardware reset or a USB bus reset. USBHS_DEVEPTCFGx, USBHS_DEVEPTISRx and USBHS_DEVEPTIMRx reset, while the configuration (ALLOC, EPBK, EPSIZE, EPDIR, EPTYPE in USBHS_DEVEPTCFGx) is kept.

fields.name: EPEN
fields.text: Enables endpoint x, one bit per endpoint.

values.text: Endpoint x off: it goes inactive and ignores USB requests, and USBHS_DEVEPTCFGx, USBHS_DEVEPTISRx and USBHS_DEVEPTIMRx reset, while the configuration (ALLOC, EPBK, EPSIZE, EPDIR, EPTYPE in USBHS_DEVEPTCFGx) is kept.

fields.name: FNCERR
fields.text: Flags a frame or microframe number received with a bad CRC.

values.text: A frame or microframe number arrived corrupted; updates together with the SOF or MSOF flag.

fields.name: FNUM
fields.text: The 11-bit frame number from the latest SOF packet. Updated even from a corrupted SOF; a USB reset clears it.

fields.name: MFNUM
fields.text: The 3-bit microframe number from the latest MSOF packet. Updated even from a corrupted MSOF; cleared at each SOF interrupt or by a USB reset.

fields.name: NBTRANS
fields.text: Transactions per microframe for a high-bandwidth isochronous endpoint. Writable only on endpoints with that capability (USBHS_FEATURES.ENHBISOx), otherwise 0; no meaning for other endpoint types.

values.name: 0_TRANS
values.text: Reserved for endpoints without high-bandwidth isochronous support.

values.name: 2_TRANS
values.text: Two transactions per microframe; configure the endpoint with two banks.

values.name: 3_TRANS
values.text: Three transactions per microframe; configure the endpoint with three banks.

fields.name: EPTYPE
fields.text: Picks the endpoint type. A USB reset clears it.

fields.name: AUTOSW
fields.text: Turns on automatic bank switching. A USB reset clears it.

fields.name: EPDIR
fields.text: Endpoint direction: 0 (OUT) or 1 (IN); IN is not for control endpoints. A USB reset clears it.

values.name: IN
values.text: IN endpoint; not allowed on a control endpoint.

fields.name: EPSIZE
fields.text: Size of each bank of the endpoint. A USB reset clears it, except on endpoint 0.

fields.name: EPBK
fields.text: Number of banks for the endpoint; a control endpoint takes a single bank (0b00). A USB reset clears it, except on endpoint 0.

fields.name: ALLOC
fields.text: Reserves or releases the endpoint's memory. A USB reset clears it, except on endpoint 0.

values.text: Reserves the endpoint memory; check USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.CFGOK to see whether it worked.

registers.name: USBHS_DEVEPTISRx
registers.title: Device Endpoint Interrupt Status Register (Control, Bulk, Interrupt Endpoints)
notes: Used when USBHS_DEVEPTCFGx.EPTYPE is 0x0, 0x2 or 0x3.

fields.name: BYCT
fields.text: Bytes held in the FIFO. For IN it counts up on each byte software writes and down on each byte sent; for OUT up on each byte received and down on each byte software reads. It can lag RWALL by one clock, so do not poll it like an interrupt flag.

fields.name: CFGOK
fields.text: Shows, once USBHS_DEVEPTCFGx.ALLOC = 1, whether the requested EPBK and EPSIZE fit the endpoint's limits and the DPRAM. When 0, write valid EPBK and EPSIZE values again.

fields.name: CTRLDIR
fields.text: Direction of the packet after a SETUP: 0 OUT, 1 IN.

values.text: Next packet after the SETUP is OUT.
Next packet after the SETUP is IN.

fields.name: RWALL
fields.text: For IN, 1 means the current bank has room for more data; for OUT, 1 means it still holds data to read. Stays 0 on error or with USBHS_DEVEPTIMRx.STALLRQ = 1. Not for control endpoints.

fields.name: CURRBK
fields.text: Bank in use on a non-control endpoint. It can lag RWALL by one clock, so do not poll it like an interrupt flag.

fields.name: NBUSYBK
fields.text: How many banks are busy. For IN, banks filled by software and waiting to go; a PEP_x interrupt comes when all are free if NBUSYBKE = 1. For OUT, banks filled by the host; a PEP_x interrupt comes when all are busy if NBUSYBKE = 1. After FIFOCON is cleared (FIFOCONC written 1) to hand over a new bank, the count updates two or three clocks later, to work out the next bank's address.

fields.name: DTSEQ
fields.text: Data PID of the current bank. For IN, the toggle to use on the next packet sent (not tied to the current bank); for OUT, the last toggle received into the current bank. Resets to 0b01 (Data1), so Data0 comes next.

fields.name: SHORTPACKET
fields.text: Flags a short packet on a non-control OUT endpoint.

values.text: Cleared and acknowledged by writing 1 to SHORTPACKETC.
A non-control OUT endpoint received a short packet; PEP_x follows if USBHS_DEVEPTIMRx.SHORTPACKETE = 1.

fields.name: STALLEDI
fields.text: Flags that a STALL handshake went out.

values.text: Cleared and acknowledged by writing 1 to STALLEDIC.
A STALL handshake went out, which software requests by setting STALLRQ through STALLRQS; PEP_x follows if STALLEDE = 1.

fields.name: OVERFI
fields.text: Flags an overflow: in an OUT stage the host wrote a packet larger than the bank. The packet is ACKed, RXOUTI is set as usual and the bank keeps the leading bytes that fit.

values.text: Cleared and acknowledged by writing 1 to OVERFIC.
An overflow happened; PEP_x follows if OVERFE = 1.

fields.name: NAKINI
fields.text: Flags a NAK sent to an IN request.

values.text: Cleared and acknowledged by writing 1 to NAKINIC.
A NAK went out in answer to an IN request; PEP_x follows if NAKINE = 1.

fields.name: NAKOUTI
fields.text: Flags a NAK sent to an OUT request.

values.text: Cleared and acknowledged by writing 1 to NAKOUTIC.
A NAK went out in answer to an OUT request; PEP_x follows if NAKOUTE = 1.

fields.name: RXSTPI
fields.text: Set on a control endpoint when the current bank holds a new valid SETUP packet; raises PEP_x if RXSTPE = 1. Write 1 to RXSTPIC to clear it, which acknowledges and frees the bank. Stays 0 on bulk and interrupt endpoints.

fields.name: RXOUTI
fields.text: Received OUT data. Control endpoints: 0 after a 1 to RXOUTIC, which acknowledges and frees the bank; 1 when the bank holds an OUT packet (data or status stage), with PEP_x if RXOUTE = 1. Bulk and interrupt OUT: 0 after a 1 to RXOUTIC, which does not touch the FIFO and must come before FIFOCON is cleared; 1 together with FIFOCON when the bank fills, with PEP_x if RXOUTE = 1. Software reads the FIFO, then clears FIFOCON to free the bank and move to the next one; RXOUTI and FIFOCON then follow that bank. Stays 0 on bulk and interrupt IN endpoints.

values.text: A 1 to RXOUTIC clears it, acknowledging the interrupt and freeing the bank.
The bank has taken in a bulk OUT packet in the data or the status stage; PEP_x if RXOUTE = 1.

values.when: For bulk and interrupt OUT endpoints
values.text: A 1 to RXOUTIC clears it; acknowledges the interrupt without touching the FIFO.

values.when: For bulk and interrupt OUT endpoints
values.text: Set with FIFOCON when the bank fills; PEP_x if RXOUTE = 1.

fields.name: TXINI
fields.text: Transmitted IN data. Control endpoints: 0 after a 1 to TXINIC, which acknowledges and sends the packet; 1 when the bank can take a new IN packet, with PEP_x if TXINE = 1. Bulk and interrupt IN: 0 after a 1 to TXINIC, which does not touch the FIFO and must come before FIFOCON is cleared; 1 together with FIFOCON when the bank is free, with PEP_x if TXINE = 1. Software fills the FIFO, then clears FIFOCON to send and move to the next bank; TXINI and FIFOCON then follow that bank. Stays 0 on bulk and interrupt OUT endpoints.

values.text: A 1 to TXINIC clears it, acknowledging the interrupt and sending the packet.
The bank can take a new IN packet; PEP_x if TXINE = 1.

values.when: For bulk and interrupt IN endpoints
values.text: A 1 to TXINIC clears it; acknowledges the interrupt without touching the FIFO.

values.when: For bulk and interrupt IN endpoints
values.text: Set with FIFOCON when the bank is free; PEP_x if TXINE = 1.

registers.name: USBHS_DEVEPTISRx
registers.title: Device Endpoint Interrupt Status Register (Isochronous Endpoints)
notes: Used when USBHS_DEVEPTCFGx.EPTYPE is 0x1.

fields.name: BYCT
fields.text: Bytes held in the FIFO. For IN it counts up on each byte software writes and down on each byte sent; for OUT up on each byte received and down on each byte software reads. It can lag RWALL by one clock, so do not poll it like an interrupt flag.

fields.name: CFGOK
fields.text: Shows, once USBHS_DEVEPTCFGx.ALLOC = 1, whether the requested EPBK and EPSIZE fit the endpoint's limits and the DPRAM. When 0, write valid EPBK and EPSIZE values again.

fields.name: RWALL
fields.text: For IN, 1 means the current bank has room for more data; for OUT, 1 means it still holds data to read. Stays 0 on error.

fields.name: CURRBK
fields.text: Bank in use. It can lag RWALL by one clock, so do not poll it like an interrupt flag.

fields.name: NBUSYBK
fields.text: How many banks are busy. For IN, banks filled by software and waiting to go; a PEP_x interrupt comes when all are free if NBUSYBKE = 1. For OUT, banks filled by the host; a PEP_x interrupt comes when all are busy if NBUSYBKE = 1. After FIFOCON is cleared (FIFOCONC written 1) to hand over a new bank, the count updates two or three clocks later, to work out the next bank's address.

fields.name: ERRORTRANS
fields.text: Set when a transaction in the current microframe breaks the USB 2.0 data toggle sequence; raises PEP_x if USBHS_DEVEPTIMRx.ERRORTRANSE = 1. Stays set while CURRBK points into the bad group of n transactions (n = 1, 2 or 3); software clears it by clearing USBHS_DEVEPTIMRx.FIFOCON at least once to reach the next microframe's banks.

fields.name: DTSEQ
fields.text: Data PID of the current bank. For IN, the toggle to use on the next packet sent (not tied to the current bank); for OUT, the last toggle received into the current bank. Resets to 0b01 (Data1), so Data0 comes next. On a high-bandwidth isochronous endpoint PEP_x fires when MDATAE = 1 and an MData packet arrives, or DATAXE = 1 and a Data0/1/2 packet arrives (with RXOUTI = 1).

fields.name: SHORTPACKET
fields.text: Flags a short packet on a non-control OUT endpoint.

values.text: Cleared and acknowledged by writing 1 to SHORTPACKETC.
A non-control OUT endpoint received a short packet; PEP_x follows if USBHS_DEVEPTIMRx.SHORTPACKETE = 1.

fields.name: CRCERRI
fields.text: Flags a CRC error.

values.text: Cleared and acknowledged by writing 1 to CRCERRIC.
An isochronous OUT endpoint got a packet with a CRC error; the packet is stored anyway. PEP_x follows if CRCERRE = 1.

fields.name: OVERFI
fields.text: Flags an overflow.

values.text: Cleared and acknowledged by writing 1 to OVERFIC.

An overflow happened: in an OUT stage the host wrote a packet larger than the bank. The packet is ACKed, USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.RXOUTI is set as usual and the bank keeps the leading bytes that fit. PEP_x follows if OVERFE = 1.

fields.name: HBISOFLUSHI
fields.text: Flags banks flushed on a high-bandwidth isochronous IN endpoint.

values.text: Cleared and acknowledged by writing 1 to HBISOFLUSHIC.

On a high-bandwidth isochronous IN endpoint (NBTRANS = 2 or 3), fewer than N transactions finished without underflow by the end of the microframe, as when an IN token is missed; the banks are flushed to keep host and device in step. PEP_x follows if HBISOFLUSHE = 1.

fields.name: HBISOINERRI
fields.text: Flags an underflow on a high-bandwidth isochronous IN endpoint.

values.text: Cleared and acknowledged by writing 1 to HBISOINERRIC.
On a high-bandwidth isochronous IN endpoint (NBTRANS = 2 or 3), the CPU filled fewer than N banks in the microframe; PEP_x follows if HBISOINERRE = 1.

fields.name: UNDERFI
fields.text: Set on an isochronous endpoint at an underflow; raises PEP_x if UNDERFE = 1. In an IN stage the host read an empty bank and a zero-length packet went out; in an OUT stage a packet came with the bank still full and was dropped, usually because the CPU fell behind. Write 1 to UNDERFIC to clear and acknowledge.

fields.name: RXOUTI
fields.text: Received OUT data. Control endpoints: 0 after a 1 to RXOUTIC, which acknowledges and frees the bank; 1 when the bank holds an OUT packet (data or status stage), with PEP_x if RXOUTE = 1. OUT endpoints: 0 after a 1 to RXOUTIC, which does not touch the FIFO and must come before FIFOCON is cleared; 1 together with FIFOCON when the bank fills, with PEP_x if RXOUTE = 1. Software reads the FIFO, then clears FIFOCON to free the bank and move to the next one; RXOUTI and FIFOCON then follow that bank. Stays 0 on IN endpoints.

values.text: A 1 to RXOUTIC clears it, acknowledging the interrupt and freeing the bank.
The bank has taken in a bulk OUT packet in the data or the status stage; PEP_x if RXOUTE = 1.
A 1 to RXOUTIC clears it; acknowledges the interrupt without touching the FIFO.
Set with FIFOCON when the bank fills; PEP_x if RXOUTE = 1.

fields.name: TXINI
fields.text: Transmitted IN data. Control endpoints: 0 after a 1 to TXINIC, which acknowledges and sends the packet; 1 when the bank can take a new IN packet, with PEP_x if TXINE = 1. IN endpoints: 0 after a 1 to TXINIC, which does not touch the FIFO and must come before FIFOCON is cleared; 1 together with FIFOCON when the bank is free, with PEP_x if TXINE = 1. Software fills the FIFO, then clears FIFOCON to send and move to the next bank; TXINI and FIFOCON then follow that bank. Stays 0 on OUT endpoints.

values.text: A 1 to TXINIC clears it, acknowledging the interrupt and sending the packet.
The bank can take a new IN packet; PEP_x if TXINE = 1.
A 1 to TXINIC clears it; acknowledges the interrupt without touching the FIFO.
Set with FIFOCON when the bank is free; PEP_x if TXINE = 1.

registers.name: USBHS_DEVEPTIMRx
registers.title: Device Endpoint Interrupt Mask Register (Control, Bulk, Interrupt Endpoints)
notes: Used when USBHS_DEVEPTCFGx.EPTYPE is 0x0, 0x2 or 0x3.

fields.name: STALLRQ
fields.text: Asks for a STALL handshake to the host.

values.text: Cleared on a new SETUP packet or by USBHS_DEVEPTIDRx.STALLRQC = 0.
Set by USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.STALLRQS = 1; a STALL handshake is to be sent to the host.

fields.name: RSTDT
fields.text: Set by writing 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.RSTDTS; resets the data toggle so the next packet sent (IN) or received (OUT) is Data0. Clears at once, so there is no need to wait on it.

fields.name: NYETDIS
fields.text: Makes the endpoint answer ACK in place of NYET at high speed.

values.text: Cleared by USBHS_DEVEPTIDRx.NYETDISC = 1; the high-speed handshake follows USB 2.0.
Set by USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.NYETDISS = 1; at high speed an ACK goes out in place of NYET.

fields.name: EPDISHDMA
fields.text: Set by writing 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.EPDISHDMAS. Any endpoint x interrupt (PEP_x) then pauses DMA channel x, whether or not PEP_x is enabled; to finish the transfer, acknowledge or disable the source (such as RXOUTI) or clear this bit with EPDISHDMAC. In ping-pong mode, when the interrupt belongs to a new bank's packet while DMA works on the previous one, the previous transfer completes and the new one is not requested. Interrupts not tied to a new packet (NAKINI, NAKOUTI and the like) can pause the transfer at any moment. Uses include catching bad packets before they reach a buffer and finishing a DMA transfer in software after a short packet.

fields.name: FIFOCON
fields.text: Bank handover. On control endpoints FIFOCON and RWALL have no use and read 0. IN: 0 after a 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIDRx.FIFOCONC, which sends the FIFO data and moves to the next bank; 1 when the bank is free, together with TXINI. OUT: 0 after a 1 to FIFOCONC, which frees the bank and moves to the next one; 1 when the bank is full, together with RXOUTI.

values.text: A 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIDRx.FIFOCONC clears it, sending the FIFO data and moving to the next bank.
Bank free; set together with USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.TXINI.
A 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIDRx.FIFOCONC clears it, freeing the bank and moving to the next one.
Bank full; set together with USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.RXOUTI.

fields.name: KILLBK
fields.text: Set by writing 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.KILLBKS; drops the most recently written IN bank and clears when done. The kill takes effect once the USBHS core accepts it, then the bit clears. Outcomes: the bank is killed and NBUSYBK drops; the bank was already sent and NBUSYBK drops; or the bank was empty and nothing is cleared. Wait for 0 before killing another. Refused if an IN token arrives while the last bank is the one going out; with two or more banks ready, the current one is sent and the last is killed.

fields.name: NBUSYBKE
fields.text: Enables the interrupt from USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.NBUSYBK.

values.text: Cleared by USBHS_DEVEPTIDRx.NBUSYBKEC = 0; the USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.NBUSYBK interrupt is off.
Set by USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.NBUSYBKES = 1; the USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.NBUSYBK interrupt is on.

fields.name: SHORTPACKETE
fields.text: Enables the short packet interrupt. On a non-control IN endpoint, a 1 also makes a DMA transfer end with a short packet (end of isochronous frame or end of bulk or interrupt transfer), provided END_B_EN and AUTOSW are both 1.

values.text: Cleared by USBHS_DEVEPTIDRx.SHORTPACKETEC = 1; the USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.SHORTPACKET interrupt is off.
Set by USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.SHORTPACKETES = 1; the USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.SHORTPACKET interrupt is on.

fields.name: STALLEDE
fields.text: Enables the STALLed interrupt.
