fields.name: RSTDT
fields.text: Set by writing 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.RSTDTS; resets the data toggle so the next packet sent (IN) or received (OUT) is Data0. Clears at once, so there is no need to wait on it.

fields.name: EPDISHDMA
fields.text: Set by writing 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.EPDISHDMAS. Any endpoint x interrupt (PEP_x) then pauses DMA channel x, whether or not PEP_x is enabled; to finish the transfer, acknowledge or disable the source (such as RXOUTI) or clear this bit with EPDISHDMAC. In ping-pong mode, when the interrupt belongs to a new bank's packet while DMA works on the previous one, the previous transfer completes and the new one is not requested. Interrupts not tied to a new packet (NAKINI, NAKOUTI and the like) can pause the transfer at any moment. Uses include catching bad packets before they reach a buffer and finishing a DMA transfer in software after a short packet.

fields.name: FIFOCON
fields.text: Bank handover. On control endpoints FIFOCON and RWALL have no use and read 0. IN: 0 after a 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIDRx.FIFOCONC, which sends the FIFO data and moves to the next bank; 1 when the bank is free, together with TXINI. OUT: 0 after a 1 to FIFOCONC, which frees the bank and moves to the next one; 1 when the bank is full, together with RXOUTI.

values.text: A 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIDRx.FIFOCONC clears it, sending the FIFO data and moving to the next bank.
Bank free; set together with USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.TXINI.
A 1 to USBHS_DEVEPTIDRx.FIFOCONC clears it, freeing the bank and moving to the next one.
Bank full; set together with USBHS_DEVEPTISRx.RXOUTI.

fields.name: KILLBK
fields.text: Drops the most recently written IN bank. The kill takes effect once the USBHS core accepts it, then the bit clears. Outcomes: the bank is killed and NBUSYBK drops; the bank was already sent and NBUSYBK drops; or the bank was empty and nothing is cleared. Wait for 0 before killing another. Refused if an IN token arrives while the last bank is the one going out; with two or more banks ready, the current one is sent and the last is killed.

values.text: Clears once the bank is killed.
Set by USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.KILLBKS = 1; drops the most recently written bank.

registers.name: USBHS_DEVDMANXTDSCx
registers.title: Device DMA Channel x Next Descriptor Address Register

fields.name: NXT_DSC_ADD
fields.text: Address of the next channel descriptor to run. Descriptors are aligned, so bits 3:0 are 0.

registers.name: USBHS_DEVDMAADDRESSx
registers.title: Device DMA Channel x Address Register

fields.name: BUFF_ADD
fields.text: AHB address the DMA channel transfers from or to; start and end may sit on any byte. Firmware can write it only while USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS.CHANN_ENB is 0. It advances by the access width at the end of each AHB address phase; the width is 4 bytes, or fewer at a packet start or end not on a word boundary. A packet starts at the channel start address or the next address due in the buffer, and ends at the channel end address or the last address reached. Software or a descriptor load sets the start; the end comes from the buffer end, from the USB device, or from the USB end of transfer when USBHS_DEVDMACONTROLx.END_TR_EN is 1.

registers.name: USBHS_DEVDMACONTROLx
registers.title: Device DMA Channel x Control Register

fields.name: BUFF_LENGTH
fields.text: Bytes to move before the buffer ends. 0, the reset value, means the 32-Kbyte maximum; use 0 when the size is unknown, and the USB device may end the transfer sooner. A write also loads USBHS_DEVDMASTATUSx.BUFF_COUNT. Bits [31:2] take a write only with a channel command other than Stop Now. Before such a command, wait until USBHS_DEVDMASTATUSx.CHAN_ACT and CHAN_ENB both read 0 so the channel has stopped.

fields.name: BURST_LCK
fields.text: Locks the bus for the DMA's AHB bursts.

values.text: The DMA never locks the bus.
AHB bursts of a USB packet are locked, making the best use of bus bandwidth and the longest fly-by bursts.

fields.name: DESC_LD_IT
fields.text: Enables an interrupt on a descriptor load.

values.text: Interrupt once a descriptor is fetched from the bus.

fields.name: END_BUFFIT
fields.text: Enables an interrupt at the end of the buffer.

fields.name: END_TR_IT
fields.text: Enables an interrupt at the end of a transfer, for a receive of unknown size.

values.text: No interrupt when USBHS_DEVDMASTATUSx.END_TR_ST rises because the USBHS device finished the buffer transfer.
Interrupt once the buffer transfer is done, when the USBHS device ended it.

fields.name: END_B_EN
fields.text: Lets the DMA buffer end validate the packet: chiefly a short IN packet when the DMA reaches the buffer end, but also cutting off unwanted OUT data there.

values.text: The DMA buffer end does not affect the USB packet transfer.
At the DMA buffer end (USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS.BUFF_COUNT reaching 0) the endpoint can validate the packet, as set by USBHS_DEVEPTCFGx.AUTOSW and USBHS_DEVEPTIERx.SHORTPACKETES.

fields.name: END_TR_EN
fields.text: Lets the USB end of transfer close the buffer. With it set, the buffer closes on a bulk or interrupt short packet or on the final packet of an isochronous (micro)frame (DATAX), and USBHS_DEVDMASTATUSx.END_TR_ST rises. Meant for bulk or interrupt transfers whose length is not agreed beforehand, and for closing an isochronous microframe buffer.

values.text: The USB end of transfer is not acted on.
The USBHS device may end the current buffer transfer.

fields.name: LDNXT_DSC
fields.text: With CHANN_ENB, picks the channel command. With CHANN_ENB = 0 the next descriptor loads as soon as a transfer is requested.

values.text: Nothing loaded once the channel transfer ends.
Next descriptor loaded once the current transfer ends, when USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS.CHANN_ENB clears.

fields.name: CHANN_ENB
fields.text: With LDNXT_DSC, picks the channel command; turns the channel on or off.

values.text: Channel off at the end of transfer; requests start nothing. Hardware also clears it when the channel source bus shuts at the buffer end. After a descriptor load clears LDNXT_DSC, firmware sets CHANN_ENB to start the described transfer if wanted. With LDNXT_DSC = 0 the channel freezes, and its registers can be read and written safely once USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS.CHANN_ENB and CHANN_ACT both read 0. Cleared during a transfer, the DMA FIFO empties before the status CHANN_ENB clears. With LDNXT_DSC set at or after the clearing, the loaded descriptor is skipped with no data moved and the next one loads at once.
Sets USBHS_DEVDMASTATUS.CHANN_ENB so the channel moves data; any pending request then starts. Starts or resumes a requested transfer.

registers.name: USBHS_DEVDMASTATUSx
registers.title: Device DMA Channel x Status Register

fields.name: BUFF_COUNT
fields.text: Bytes still to move in this buffer. Drops by the AHB access width at the end of each address phase; that width is 4, or fewer at a DMA start or end not on a word boundary. At the buffer end the DMA reads or writes only the bytes still owed. For OUT endpoints with BUFF_LENGTH left at 0 because the length was unknown, the bytes received are 0x10000 - BUFF_COUNT.

fields.name: DESC_LDST
fields.text: Shows that a descriptor was loaded; holds until CHANN_ENB clears at the end of the following buffer.

values.text: Clears by itself when software reads it.
Hardware sets it once a descriptor is fetched from the system bus.

fields.name: END_BF_ST
fields.text: Shows that the channel buffer ended; holds until CHANN_ENB clears at the end of the following buffer.

values.text: Clears by itself when software reads it.
Hardware sets it when BUFF_COUNT counts down to 0.

fields.name: END_TR_ST
fields.text: Shows that the channel transfer ended; holds until CHANN_ENB clears at the end of the following buffer.

values.text: Clears by itself when software reads it.
Hardware sets it when the last packet transfer is done, if the USBHS device ended the transfer.

fields.name: CHANN_ACT
fields.text: Shows the channel is busy moving packet data. Clears when a packet transfer ends. If END_BF_ST stops a packet short, it stays set through the next descriptor load (if any) and possibly until a USBHS packet transfer completes, when the new descriptor allows it.

values.text: The channel has stopped trying to source packet data.
The channel is trying to source packet data, being the highest-priority requester.

fields.name: CHANN_ENB
fields.text: Shows whether the channel is on. Clears by itself when a transfer ends by byte count or because the USBHS device ended it. Normally follows USBHS_DEVDMACONTROLx.CHANN_ENB as written by software or a descriptor load; if that bit clears during a transfer, the DMA FIFO empties first, then this bit clears.

values.text: The channel stops moving data and can fetch the next descriptor when USBHS_DEVDMACONTROLx.LDNXT_DSC is 1.
The channel is on and moves data when asked.

fields.name: SPDCONF
fields.text: Sets the speeds the host can run at.

values.name: NORMAL
values.text: Starts at full speed and moves to high speed through a high-speed reset when the peripheral supports it.

values.name: LOW_POWER
values.text: Low power: for use when high speed is not needed.

values.name: FORCED_FS
values.text: Stays at full speed whatever the peripheral supports.

fields.name: RESUME
fields.text: Write 1 to send a USB resume; only while SOF generation is on (SOFE = 1). Clears once the resume is out or a USB reset is asked for.

values.text: Sends a USB resume on the bus.

fields.name: RESET
fields.text: Write 1 to send a USB reset; clears once it has gone out. Writing 0 can be used if the device disconnects (USBHS_HSTISR.DDISCI = 1) during the reset.

values.text: Sends a USB reset on the bus.

fields.name: SOFE
fields.text: Turns on SOF generation. Set by hardware when a USB reset is asked for or an upstream resume is seen (USBHS_HSTISR.TXRSMI).

values.text: No SOF; the bus is left idle.
Sends SOF at full or high speed, and keep-alive at low speed.

fields.name: DMA_7
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 7.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS7 source is cleared.
DMA channel 7 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_HSTIMR.DMA_7 = 1.

fields.name: DMA_6
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 6.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS6 source is cleared.

fields.name: DMA_5

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS5 source is cleared.

fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 4.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS4 source is cleared.
DMA channel 4 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_HSTIMR.DMA_4 = 1.

fields.name: DMA_3
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 3.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS3 source is cleared.
DMA channel 3 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_HSTIMR.DMA_3 = 1.

fields.name: DMA_2
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 2.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS2 source is cleared.

fields.name: DMA_1
fields.text: Interrupt flag of DMA channel 1.

values.text: Clears once the USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS1 source is cleared.
DMA channel 1 raised an interrupt; a USB interrupt follows if USBHS_HSTIMR.DMA_1 = 1.

fields.name: PEP_
fields.text: Interrupt flag of pipe x, one bit per pipe.

values.text: Clears once the source is handled.
Pipe x raised an interrupt (USBHS_HSTPIPISRx); a USB interrupt follows if the matching USBHS_HSTIMR bit is 1.

fields.name: HWUPI
fields.text: Host wakeup: set while the host is suspended (SOFE = 0) and the peripheral sends an upstream resume or disconnects. Raised even with the clock frozen by USBHS_CTRL.FRZCLK.

fields.name: HSOFI
fields.text: Flags a SOF sent by the host.

values.text: The host sent a SOF; a USB interrupt follows if HSOFE = 1. At low speed a keep-alive also sets it.

fields.name: RXRSMI
fields.text: Flags an upstream resume from the device.

values.text: An upstream resume came from the device.

fields.name: RSMEDI
fields.text: Flags a downstream resume sent to the device.

fields.name: PRST
fields.text: Resets pipe x, one bit per pipe.

values.text: Ends the reset; the FIFO can be used.

Resets the pipe x FIFO: USBHS_HSTPIPCFGx, USBHS_HSTPIPISRx and USBHS_HSTPIPIMRx reset, while the configuration (INTFRQ, PEPNUM, PTYPE, PTOKEN, PSIZE, PBK, ALLOC) is kept. The FIFO counter, reception and transmission start over, data toggle handling excepted; the pipe stays configured and enabled.

fields.name: PEN
fields.text: Enables pipe x, one bit per pipe.

values.text: Pipe x off: it goes inactive, and USBHS_HSTPIPCFGx, USBHS_HSTPIPISRx and USBHS_HSTPIPIMRx reset, while the configuration (ALLOC, PBK, PSIZE in USBHS_HSTPIPCFGx) is kept.

registers.name: USBHS_HSTPIPCFGx
registers.title: Host Pipe x Configuration Register
notes: A high-speed bulk-out pipe uses its own layout of this register.

fields.name: INTFRQ
fields.text: Longest polling period of an interrupt pipe, in ms; no effect on other pipe types. Cleared when a USB reset is sent.

fields.name: PEPNUM
fields.text: Endpoint number the pipe talks to, 0 to 9. Cleared when a USB reset is sent.

fields.name: PTYPE
fields.text: Pipe type. Cleared when a USB reset is sent.

fields.name: AUTOSW
fields.text: Turns on automatic bank switching. Cleared when a USB reset is sent.

fields.name: PTOKEN
fields.text: Token the pipe sends.

fields.name: PSIZE
fields.text: Size of each bank of the pipe. Cleared when a USB reset is sent.

fields.name: PBK
fields.text: Number of banks for the pipe; a control pipe takes a single bank (0b00). Cleared when a USB reset is sent.

fields.name: ALLOC
fields.text: Reserves or releases the pipe's memory. Cleared when a USB reset is asked for.

registers.name: USBHS_HSTPIPCFGx
registers.title: Host Pipe x Configuration Register (High-speed Bulk-out or High-speed Control Pipe)
notes: Used when USBHS_HSTPIPCFGx.PTYPE is 0x0 or 0x2.

fields.name: BINTERVAL
fields.text: Interval for PING or bulk-out tokens, 0 to 255. With PINGEN = 1: above 0, one PING every bInterval microframes until ACKed; 0, back-to-back PINGs in one microframe until ACKed. With PINGEN = 0: the same pattern with OUT tokens.

fields.name: PINGEN
fields.text: Turns on the ping protocol; applies only to high-speed bulk-out, including the data and status stages of control transfers. Cleared when a USB reset is sent.

values.text: Ping protocol on, as USB 2.0 defines it.

notes: Used when USBHS_HSTPIPCFGx.PTYPE is 0x0 or 0x2.

fields.name: PBYCT
fields.text: Bytes held in the FIFO. For OUT it counts up on each byte software writes and down on each byte sent; for IN up on each byte received and down on each byte software reads. It can lag RWALL by one clock, so do not poll it like an interrupt flag.

fields.name: CFGOK
fields.text: Updated when USBHS_HSTPIPCFGx.ALLOC is set; 1 if PBK and PSIZE fit the pipe's limits and the DPRAM. When 0, write valid PBK and PSIZE values again.

fields.name: RWALL
fields.text: For OUT, 1 means the current bank has room for more data; for IN, 1 means it still holds data to read. Also 0 when RXSTALLDI or PERRI is 1.

fields.name: CURRBK
fields.text: Bank in use on a non-control pipe. It can lag RWALL by one clock, so do not poll it like an interrupt flag.

fields.name: NBUSYBK
fields.text: How many banks are busy. For OUT, banks filled by software and waiting to go; a PEP_x interrupt comes when all are busy if USBHS_HSTPIPIMRx.NBUSYBKE = 1. For IN, banks filled from the device; a PEP_x interrupt comes when all are free if NBUSYBKE = 1.

fields.name: DTSEQ
fields.text: Data PID of the current bank: for OUT, the toggle of the next packet to send; for IN, the toggle of the packet held in the bank.

fields.name: SHORTPACKETI
fields.text: Flags a short packet received.

values.text: The host received a short packet, shorter than PSIZE.

fields.name: RXSTALLDI
fields.text: Set when the current bank receives a STALL handshake; the pipe freezes, and an interrupt follows if USBHS_HSTPIPIMR.RXSTALLE = 1.

fields.name: OVERFI
fields.text: Flags an overflow.

values.text: The pipe received more data than its maximum length; an interrupt follows if USBHS_HSTPIPIMR.OVERFIE = 1.

fields.name: NAKEDI
fields.text: Flags a NAK received.

values.text: The current bank received a NAK; an interrupt follows if USBHS_HSTPIPIMR.NAKEDE = 1.

fields.name: PERRI
fields.text: Flags an error on the pipe.

values.text: Clears once the bit naming the error is cleared.

fields.name: TXSTPI

fields.name: RXINI
fields.text: Flags IN data received.

values.text: A new USB message landed in the current bank; an interrupt follows if USBHS_HSTPIPIMR.RXINE = 1.

fields.name: RSTDT
fields.text: Resets the pipe's data toggle.

values.text: No data toggle reset in progress.
Set by USBHS_HSTPIPIER.RSTDTS = 1; the pipe's data toggle goes back to its start value.

fields.name: PFREEZE
fields.text: Freezes the pipe so it makes no requests.

values.text: Cleared by USBHS_HSTPIPIDR.PFREEZEC = 1; the pipe makes requests again.

Set by any of: USBHS_HSTPIPIER.PFREEZES written; the pipe not configured; a STALL received; a pipe error (USBHS_HSTPIPISR.PERRI = 1); INRQ+1 IN requests done; a rising USBHS_HSTPIP.PRSTx (pipe reset); a rising USBHS_HSTPIP.PEN (pipe enable).

fields.name: PDISHDMA
fields.text: Pauses the pipe's DMA on a pipe interrupt, in the same way as USBHS_DEVEPTIMR.EPDISHDMA does for endpoints.

fields.name: FIFOCON
fields.text: Bank handover. OUT and SETUP: 0 after USBHS_HSTPIPIDR.FIFOCONC = 1, which sends the FIFO data and moves to the next bank; 1 when the bank is free, together with TXOUTI or TXSTPI. IN: 0 after FIFOCONC = 1, which frees the bank and moves to the next one; 1 when a new IN message lands in the bank, together with USBHS_HSTPIPISR.RXINI.

values.text: USBHS_HSTPIPIDR.FIFOCONC = 1 clears it, sending the FIFO data and moving to the next bank.
Bank free; set together with USBHS_HSTPIPISR.TXOUTI or TXSTPI.
USBHS_HSTPIPIDR.FIFOCONC = 1 clears it, freeing the bank and moving to the next one.
A new IN message is in the bank; set together with USBHS_HSTPIPISR.RXINI.

fields.name: INMODE
fields.text: Picks between a set count of IN requests and an endless stream.

values.text: Sends a set number of IN requests, given by INRQ.
Sends IN requests without end while the pipe is not frozen.

fields.name: INRQ
fields.text: IN requests before the pipe freezes: the USBHS sends INRQ+1 of them, counting down by 1 after each successful one. Ignored when INMODE = 1.

registers.name: USBHS_HSTPIPERRx
registers.title: Host Pipe x Error Register
notes: A 0 written to a bit or field clears it; a 1 does nothing.

fields.name: COUNTER
fields.text: Counts errors (CRC16, TIMEOUT, PID, DATAPID or DATATGL) and resets on an error-free packet. At 3 errors in a row the pipe freezes (USBHS_HSTPIPIMRx.PFREEZE set).

fields.name: CRC16
fields.text: CRC16 error flag.

values.text: No CRC16 error since this bit was last cleared.
Hardware sets it on a CRC16 error.

fields.name: TIMEOUT
fields.text: Time-out error flag.

values.text: No time-out since this bit was last cleared.
Hardware sets it on a time-out.

fields.name: PID
fields.text: PID error flag.

values.text: No PID error since this bit was last cleared.
Hardware sets it on a PID error.

fields.name: DATAPID
fields.text: Data PID error flag.

values.text: No data PID error since this bit was last cleared.
Hardware sets it on a data PID error.

fields.name: DATATGL
fields.text: Data toggle error flag.

values.text: No data toggle error since this bit was last cleared.
Hardware sets it on a data toggle error.

registers.title: Host DMA Channel x Address Register

fields.name: BUFF_ADD
fields.text: AHB address the DMA channel transfers from or to; start and end may sit on any byte. Firmware can write it only while USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS.CHANN_ENB is 0. It advances by the access width at the end of each AHB address phase; the width is 4 bytes, or fewer at a packet start or end not on a word boundary. A packet starts at the channel start address or the next address due in the buffer, and ends at the channel end address or the last address reached. Software or a descriptor load sets the start; the end comes from the buffer end, from the USB device, or from the USB end of transfer when USBHS_HSTDMACONTROLx.END_TR_EN is 1.

registers.name: USBHS_HSTDMACONTROLx
registers.title: Host DMA Channel x Control Register

fields.name: BUFF_LENGTH
fields.text: Bytes to move before the buffer ends. 0, the reset value, means the 32-Kbyte maximum; use 0 when the size is unknown, and the USB device may end the transfer sooner. A write also loads USBHS_HSTDMASTATUSx.BUFF_COUNT. Bits [31:2] take a write only with a channel command other than Stop Now. Before such a command, wait until USBHS_HSTDMASTATUSx.CHAN_ACT and CHAN_ENB both read 0 so the channel has stopped.

fields.name: BURST_LCK
fields.text: Locks the bus for the DMA's AHB bursts.

values.text: The DMA never locks the bus.
AHB bursts of a USB packet are locked, making the best use of bus bandwidth and the longest fly-by bursts.

fields.name: DESC_LD_IT
fields.text: Enables an interrupt on a descriptor load.

values.text: Interrupt once a descriptor is fetched from the bus.

fields.name: END_BUFFIT
fields.text: Enables an interrupt at the end of the buffer.

fields.name: END_TR_IT
fields.text: Enables an interrupt at the end of a transfer, for a receive of unknown size.

values.text: No interrupt when USBHS_HSTDMASTATUSx.END_TR_ST rises because the USBHS device finished the buffer transfer.
Interrupt once the buffer transfer is done, when the USBHS device ended it.

fields.name: END_B_EN
fields.text: Lets the DMA buffer end validate the packet: chiefly a short OUT packet when the DMA reaches the buffer end, but also cutting off unwanted IN data there.

values.text: The DMA buffer end does not affect the USB packet transfer.
At the DMA buffer end (USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS.BUFF_COUNT reaching 0) the pipe can validate the packet, as set by USBHS_HSTPIPCFGx.AUTOSW and USBHS_HSTPIPIMRx.SHORTPACKETIE.

fields.name: END_TR_EN
fields.text: Lets the USB end of transfer close the buffer: a bulk or interrupt short packet closes it and raises USBHS_HSTDMASTATUSx.END_TR_ST. Meant for transfers whose size is not agreed beforehand.

values.text: The USB end of transfer is not acted on.
The USBHS device may end the current buffer transfer.

fields.name: LDNXT_DSC
fields.text: With CHANN_ENB, picks the channel command. With CHANN_ENB = 0 the next descriptor loads as soon as a transfer is requested.

values.text: Nothing loaded once the channel transfer ends.
Next descriptor loaded once the current transfer ends, when USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS.CHANN_ENB clears.

fields.name: CHANN_ENB
fields.text: With LDNXT_DSC, picks the channel command; turns the channel on or off. After a descriptor load clears LDNXT_DSC, firmware sets CHANN_ENB to start the described transfer if wanted. With LDNXT_DSC = 0 the channel freezes, and its registers can be read and written safely once USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS.CHANN_ENB and CHANN_ACT both read 0. Cleared during a transfer, the DMA FIFO empties before the status CHANN_ENB clears. With LDNXT_DSC set at or after the clearing, the loaded descriptor is skipped with no data moved and the next one loads at once.

values.text: Channel off; requests start nothing. Hardware also clears it when the channel source bus shuts at the buffer end.
Sets USBHS_HSTDMASTATUS.CHANN_ENB so the channel moves data; any pending request then starts. Starts or resumes a requested transfer.

registers.name: USBHS_HSTDMASTATUSx
registers.title: Host DMA Channel x Status Register

fields.name: BUFF_COUNT
fields.text: Bytes still to move in this buffer. Drops by the AHB access width at the end of each address phase; that width is 4, or fewer at a DMA start or end not on a word boundary. At the buffer end the DMA reads or writes only the bytes still owed. For IN pipes with USBHS_HSTDMACONTROL.BUFF_LENGTH left at 0 because the length was unknown, the bytes received are 0x10000 - BUFF_COUNT.

fields.name: DESC_LDST
fields.text: Shows that a descriptor was loaded; holds until CHANN_ENB clears at the end of the following buffer.

values.text: Clears by itself when software reads it.
Hardware sets it once a descriptor is fetched from the system bus.

fields.name: END_BF_ST
fields.text: Shows that the channel buffer ended; holds until CHANN_ENB clears at the end of the following buffer.

values.text: Clears by itself when software reads it.
Hardware sets it when BUFF_COUNT counts down to 0.

fields.name: END_TR_ST
fields.text: Shows that the channel transfer ended; holds until CHANN_ENB clears at the end of the following buffer.

values.text: Clears by itself when software reads it.
Hardware sets it when the last packet transfer is done, if the USBHS device ended the transfer.

fields.name: CHANN_ACT
fields.text: Shows the channel is busy moving packet data. Clears when a packet transfer ends. If END_BF_ST stops a packet short, it stays set through the next descriptor load (if any) and possibly until a USBHS packet transfer completes, when the new descriptor allows it.

values.text: The channel has stopped trying to source packet data.
The channel is trying to source packet data, being the highest-priority requester.

fields.name: CHANN_ENB
fields.text: Shows whether the channel is on. Clears by itself when a transfer ends by byte count or because the USBHS device ended it. Normally follows USBHS_HSTDMACONTROLx.CHANN_ENB as written by software or a descriptor load; if that bit clears during a transfer, the DMA FIFO empties first, then this bit clears.

values.text: The channel stops moving data and can fetch the next descriptor when USBHS_HSTDMACONTROLx.LDNXT_DSC is 1.
The channel is on and moves data when asked.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to reset the HSMCI by hardware from software.

fields.name: PWSDIS
fields.text: Write 1 to turn Power Saving Mode off.

values.text: Power Saving Mode is turned off.

fields.name: PWSEN
fields.text: Write 1 to turn Power Saving Mode on; HSMCI_MR.PWSDIV must first hold a nonzero value.

values.text: Power Saving Mode is turned on, provided PWSDIS is 0.

fields.name: MCIDIS
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Multi-Media Interface off.

values.text: The Multi-Media Interface is turned off.

fields.name: MCIEN
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the Multi-Media Interface on.

values.text: The Multi-Media Interface is turned on, provided MCIDIS is 0.

registers.name: HSMCI_MR
registers.title: HSMCI Mode Register
notes: Writable only while HSMCI_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: CLKODD
fields.text: Lowest bit of the clock divider, giving whether the divider is odd or even.

fields.name: PADV
fields.text: Byte written as padding in a write transfer; applies only to manual transfer.

fields.name: FBYTE
fields.text: Allows byte-wide transfers so blocks whose size is not a multiple of 4 can be moved; the meaning of BLKLEN depends on it.

fields.name: WRPROOF
fields.text: When set, the HSMCI clock is halted during a write while the internal FIFO is full, protecting data integrity at the cost of bandwidth.

fields.name: RDPROOF
fields.text: When set, the HSMCI clock is halted during a read while the internal FIFO is full, protecting data integrity at the cost of bandwidth.

fields.name: PWSDIV
fields.text: In Power Saving Mode the interface clock is divided by 2^PWSDIV + 1; must be nonzero before HSMCI_CR.PWSEN is set.

fields.name: CLKDIV
fields.text: Divider for the interface clock (MCCK, HSMCI_CK): MCK / (2 x CLKDIV + CLKODD + 2).

registers.name: HSMCI_DTOR
registers.title: HSMCI Data Timeout Register
notes: Writable only while HSMCI_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: DTOMUL
fields.text: Multiplier applied to DTOCYC to form the data time-out; exceeding it raises HSMCI_SR.DTOE.

fields.name: DTOCYC
fields.text: Cycle count of the data time-out: the longest wait, in Host Clock cycles, between two data block transfers is DTOCYC times the DTOMUL multiplier.

registers.name: HSMCI_SDCR
registers.title: HSMCI SDCard/SDIO Register
notes: Writable only while HSMCI_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: SDCBUS
fields.text: Width of the SD card / SDIO data bus.

fields.name: SDCSEL
fields.text: Selects the SD card / SDIO slot.

fields.name: ARG
fields.text: Argument sent with the command.

registers.name: HSMCI_CMDR
registers.title: HSMCI Command Register
notes: Locked against writes while HSMCI_SR.CMDRDY is 0.
Once an Interrupt command has been sent, the only write accepted is an interrupt response (SPCMD), so the command under way cannot be stopped or altered.

fields.name: BOOT_ACK
fields.text: When 1, a boot acknowledge from the device is expected after a Boot Request command, within the time set by HSMCI_DTOR.DTOMUL and DTOCYC; a missing acknowledge raises an acknowledge time-out error and a corrupted one an acknowledge pattern error.

fields.name: ATACS
fields.text: 0 (NORMAL): normal operation; 1 (COMPLETION): a completion signal is expected within the time set in HSMCI_CSTOR.

values.name: COMPLETION
values.text: A completion signal is expected within the time set in HSMCI_CSTOR.

fields.name: IOSPCMD
fields.text: Marks the command as an SDIO special command.

fields.name: TRTYP
fields.text: Kind of data transfer the command performs.

fields.name: TRDIR
fields.text: Direction of the data transfer: 0 (WRITE) write, 1 (READ) read.

fields.name: TRCMD
fields.text: Data transfer action started with the command.

fields.name: MAXLAT
fields.text: Longest wait from command to response: 0 (5) 5 cycles, 1 (64) 64 cycles.

fields.name: OPDCMD
fields.text: Command line drive: 0 (PUSHPULL) push-pull, 1 (OPENDRAIN) open drain.

fields.name: SPCMD
fields.text: Special action of the command.

values.name: SYNC
values.text: Synchronized command: the pending command waits until the current data block has finished.

values.name: CE_ATA
values.text: CE-ATA completion signal disable: the host removes the device's ability to signal command completion on the command line.

values.name: BOR
values.text: Boot operation request: starts boot mode, in which the host reads boot data straight from the MMC device.

values.name: EBO
values.text: End boot operation: the host ends boot mode.

fields.name: RSPTYP
fields.text: Kind of response expected.

fields.name: CMDNB
fields.text: Index of the command.

fields.name: BLKLEN
fields.text: Size of a data block; bits 16 and 17 must be 0 when FBYTE is off; unused in SDIO byte mode.

fields.name: BCNT
fields.text: Number of blocks or bytes to move; allowed values follow HSMCI_CMDR.TRTYP. TRTYP = 1 (MMC/SD multiple block): 1 to 65535, 0 means an endless block transfer. TRTYP = 4 (SDIO byte): 1 to 511, 0 means 512 bytes, 512 to 65536 not allowed. TRTYP = 5 (SDIO block): 1 to 511, 0 means an endless block transfer, 512 to 65536 not allowed. With TRTYP = 4 or 5, a nonzero value in the top 7 bits is not allowed and gives unpredictable results.

registers.name: HSMCI_CSTOR
registers.title: HSMCI Completion Signal Timeout Register
notes: Writable only while HSMCI_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: CSTOMUL
fields.text: Multiplier applied to CSTOCYC to form the completion signal time-out: the longest wait, in Host Clock cycles, from the end of the data transfer (data phase plus any busy phase) to the completion signal, or from the end of the response for a non-DATA ATA command; exceeding it raises HSMCI_SR.CSTOE.

fields.name: CSTOCYC
fields.text: Cycle count of the completion signal time-out, in Host Clock cycles, multiplied by the CSTOMUL multiplier.

fields.name: RSP
fields.text: Response word; a response of up to 128 bits is read across the four registers at 0x20, 0x24, 0x28 and 0x2C.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Data read from the card.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Data written to the card.

registers.name: HSMCI_SR
registers.title: HSMCI Status Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xC0E5.

fields.name: UNRE
fields.text: Underrun flag; with HSMCI_CFG.FERRCTRL = 1 it clears when read, with FERRCTRL = 0 it clears on a write to HSMCI_CMDR.

values.text: At least one 8-bit datum was sent that had not been written, carrying no valid data.

fields.name: OVRE
fields.text: Overrun flag; with HSMCI_CFG.FERRCTRL = 1 it clears when read, with FERRCTRL = 0 it clears on a write to HSMCI_CMDR.

values.text: At least one received 8-bit datum was lost before being read.

fields.name: ACKRCVE
fields.text: Boot acknowledge error flag; clears when read.

values.text: No boot operation error since HSMCI_SR was last read.
A corrupted boot acknowledge was received since HSMCI_SR was last read.

fields.name: ACKRCV
fields.text: Boot acknowledge received flag; clears when read.

values.text: No boot acknowledge since HSMCI_SR was last read.
A boot acknowledge was received since HSMCI_SR was last read.

fields.name: XFRDONE
fields.text: Transfer done flag.

values.text: The command register is ready and the data bus is idle.

fields.name: FIFOEMPTY
fields.text: FIFO empty flag.

values.text: The FIFO holds one byte or more.

fields.name: BLKOVRE
fields.text: DMA block overrun error flag; clears when read.

values.text: A new data block arrived before the DMA controller began moving the pending block.

fields.name: CSTOE
fields.text: Completion signal time-out error flag; clears when read.

values.text: The completion signal time-out from HSMCI_CSTOR.CSTOCYC and CSTOMUL was exceeded.

fields.name: DTOE
fields.text: Data time-out error flag; clears when read.

values.text: The data time-out from HSMCI_DTOR.DTOCYC and DTOMUL was exceeded.

fields.name: DCRCE
fields.text: Data CRC error flag; clears when read.

values.text: A CRC16 error was found in the last data block.

fields.name: RTOE
fields.text: Response time-out error flag; clears on a write to HSMCI_CMDR.

values.text: The response time-out set by HSMCI_CMDR.MAXLAT was exceeded.

fields.name: RENDE
fields.text: Response end bit error flag; clears on a write to HSMCI_CMDR.

values.text: The response's end bit was not seen.

fields.name: RCRCE
fields.text: Response CRC error flag; clears on a write to HSMCI_CMDR.

values.text: A CRC7 error was found in the response.

fields.name: RDIRE
fields.text: Response direction error flag; clears on a write to HSMCI_CMDR.

values.text: The card-to-host direction bit was not seen in the response.

fields.name: RINDE
fields.text: Response index error flag; clears on a write to HSMCI_CMDR.

values.text: The index in the response differs from the index of the command sent.

fields.name: CSRCV
fields.text: CE-ATA completion signal received flag; clears when read.

values.text: No completion signal since the status was last read.
The device signalled command completion on the command line.

fields.name: SDIOWAIT
fields.text: SDIO read wait status.

values.text: The data bus is in IO wait state.

fields.name: SDIOIRQA
fields.text: SDIO interrupt on slot A flag; clears when read.

values.text: No SDIO interrupt seen on slot A.
An SDIO interrupt occurred on slot A.

fields.name: NOTBUSY
fields.text: Not busy flag. During a block write, a card with no free receive buffer holds DAT0 low and releases it once a buffer for the set block length is free. For reads it clears at the end of the host command and sets at the end of CMD12 (infinite multiple block read), at the end of the data block (single block read), or at the end of the last block (multiple block read with a set block count).

values.text: Not ready for a new data transfer; clears at the end of the card response.
Ready for a new data transfer; sets once the card stops signalling busy on the data line, meaning it has a free receive buffer.

fields.name: DTIP
fields.text: Data transfer in progress flag; clears when the CRC16 calculation ends.

values.text: A data transfer, CRC16 calculation included, is still under way.

fields.name: BLKE
fields.text: Data block ended flag; clears when read; for write operations only.

values.text: The data block transfer has not finished.
A data block transfer ended, CRC16 status transmission included; sets for every CRC status sent.

fields.name: TXRDY
fields.text: Transmit ready flag; clears on a write to HSMCI_TDR.

values.text: The last data written to HSMCI_TDR has not yet moved to the shift register.
The last data written to HSMCI_TDR has moved to the shift register.

fields.name: RXRDY
fields.text: Receive ready flag; clears on a read of HSMCI_RDR.

values.text: Nothing received since HSMCI_RDR was last read.
Data received since HSMCI_RDR was last read.

fields.name: CMDRDY
fields.text: Command ready flag; clears on a write to HSMCI_CMDR.

values.text: The last command has been sent.

registers.name: HSMCI_DMA
registers.title: HSMCI DMA Configuration Register
notes: Writable only while HSMCI_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: DMAEN
fields.text: Turns DMA hardware handshaking on.

values.text: DMA interface on; it must be off while the CPU performs transfers, or behaviour is unpredictable.

fields.name: CHKSIZE
fields.text: How many data are ready at the moment the DMA chunk request is raised.

registers.name: HSMCI_CFG
registers.title: HSMCI Configuration Register
notes: Writable only while HSMCI_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: LSYNC
fields.text: Chooses when a pending command is sent relative to the block transfer.

values.text: Sent once the data block now under way has finished.
Sent once the whole block transfer finishes, provided its length is finite (nonzero block count).

fields.name: HSMODE
fields.text: Turns high speed bus timing on.

values.text: The host drives command and data lines on rising card clock edges; the host driver must confirm in the card registers that high speed is supported.

fields.name: FERRCTRL
fields.text: Chooses how the underflow and overflow flags are cleared.

values.text: A new write or read command clears the flag.
Reading the status clears the flag.

fields.name: FIFOMODE
fields.text: Chooses when a write transfer starts from the internal FIFO. With block length at least 3/4 of the FIFO, it starts once half the FIFO is filled; at least half, once a quarter is filled; otherwise, once all the data is in the FIFO.

values.text: Starts once enough data is in the FIFO.
Starts as soon as one datum is in the FIFO.

fields.name: WPKEY
fields.text: Key that must accompany a write to WPEN.

values.name: PASSWD
values.text: The key; writing any other value cancels the write to WPEN. Reads as 0.

fields.name: WPEN
fields.text: Turns write protection of the protectable registers on or off.

values.text: Write protection off, when WPKEY is 0x4D4349 ("MCI" in ASCII).
Write protection on, when WPKEY is 0x4D4349 ("MCI" in ASCII).

fields.name: WPVSRC
fields.text: When WPVS = 1, the offset of the register a write was attempted to.

fields.name: WPVS
fields.text: Write protection violation flag.

values.text: No write protection violation since HSMCI_WPSR was last read.
A write protection violation occurred since HSMCI_WPSR was last read; an attempted write to a protected register has its offset recorded in WPVSRC.

registers.name: HSMCI_FIFOx
registers.title: HSMCI FIFOx Memory Aperture
notes: Also listed under the name HSMCI_FIFOx[x=0..255].

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Data read or data written through the FIFO.

registers.name: SPI_CR
registers.title: SPI Control Register
notes: Writable only while WPCREN is 0 in SPI_WPMR.

fields.name: LASTXFER
fields.text: Write 1 to end the transfer after the current character.

values.text: The current NPCS deasserts once the character in TD has been sent; with SPI_CSRx.CSAAT set, the exchange with the current peripheral can be ended by raising its NPCS line as soon as the TD transfer finishes.

fields.name: REQCLR
fields.text: Write 1 to restart the comparison trigger.

values.text: The comparison trigger restarts so SPI_RDR can be loaded.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to reset the SPI by hardware from software; afterwards it is in Client mode.

fields.name: SPIDIS
fields.text: Write 1 to stop the SPI once the current transmission ends: a transfer under way finishes shifting out but no new one starts, even with SPI_THR loaded. Writing SPIEN and SPIDIS both as 1 disables the SPI.

fields.name: SPIEN
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the SPI.

values.text: The SPI is enabled to send and receive.

registers.name: SPI_MR
registers.title: SPI Mode Register
notes: Writable only while SPI_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: DLYBCS
fields.text: Delay from one NPCS going inactive to the next going active, keeping chip selects from overlapping and avoiding bus contention with slow-releasing peripherals. Below 6, six peripheral clock periods are used; otherwise DLYBCS = delay x fperipheral clock.

fields.name: PCS
fields.text: Chip select used in fixed peripheral select (PS = 0). With SPI_MR.PCSDEC = 0: PCS xxx0 drives NPCS[3:0] = 1110, xx01 gives 1101, x011 gives 1011, 0111 gives 0111, 1111 is not allowed (no peripheral selected), x = don't care. With PCSDEC = 1, NPCS[3:0] outputs equal PCS.

fields.name: LLB
fields.text: Turns local loopback of the data shift register on, MISO tied internally to MOSI; for testing in Host mode only.

fields.name: WDRBT
fields.text: Makes a Host mode transfer wait for SPI_RDR to be empty.

values.text: No effect; in Host mode a transfer may start whatever the state of SPI_RDR.
In Host mode a transfer starts only when SPI_RDR holds no unread data, preventing receive overrun.

fields.name: MODFDIS
fields.text: Turns mode fault detection off.

fields.name: PCSDEC
fields.text: Lets the four NPCS lines drive an external 4-to-16 decoder for up to 15 chip selects. SPI_CSR0 sets chip selects 0 to 3, SPI_CSR1 4 to 7, SPI_CSR2 8 to 11, SPI_CSR3 12 to 14.

values.text: Each chip select line connects straight to a peripheral.
The four NPCS lines feed a 4-to-16 decoder.

fields.name: PS
fields.text: Chooses fixed or variable peripheral select.

fields.name: MSTR
fields.text: Chooses Host or Client mode.

fields.name: PCS
fields.text: In Host mode, the NPCS pin levels at the end of the transfer; reads 0 otherwise. In variable peripheral select (SPI_MR.PS = 1), SPI_MR.WDRBT must be set if this field is to be used.

fields.name: RD
fields.text: Received data, right-justified; unused bits read 0.

fields.name: LASTXFER
fields.text: Ends the transfer after this character; used only in variable peripheral select (SPI_MR.PS = 1).

values.text: The current NPCS deasserts once the character in TD has been sent; with SPI_CSRx.CSAAT set, the exchange with the current peripheral can be ended by raising its NPCS line as soon as the TD transfer finishes.

fields.name: PCS
fields.text: Chip select for this character; used only in variable peripheral select (SPI_MR.PS = 1). With SPI_MR.PCSDEC = 0: PCS xxx0 drives NPCS[3:0] = 1110, xx01 gives 1101, x011 gives 1011, 0111 gives 0111, 1111 is not allowed (no peripheral selected), x = don't care. With PCSDEC = 1, NPCS[3:0] outputs equal PCS.

fields.name: TD
fields.text: Data to send, written right-justified.

fields.name: SPIENS
fields.text: Shows whether the SPI is enabled.

fields.name: UNDES
fields.text: Underrun error flag, Client mode only; clears when read.

values.text: No underrun since SPI_SR was last read.
A transfer began with no data loaded in SPI_TDR.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Transmit registers empty flag; clears on a write to SPI_TDR.

values.text: Clears as soon as SPI_TDR is written.
SPI_TDR and the shift register are both empty; with a transfer delay set, it sets once that delay ends.

fields.name: NSSR
fields.text: NSS rising edge flag; clears when read.

values.text: No rising edge on NSS since SPI_SR was last read.
NSS saw a rising edge since SPI_SR was last read.

fields.name: OVRES
fields.text: Overrun error flag; clears when read. An overrun is SPI_RDR being loaded from the shift register two or more times without SPI_RDR being read.

values.text: No overrun since SPI_SR was last read.
An overrun occurred since SPI_SR was last read.

fields.name: MODF
fields.text: Mode fault error flag; clears when read.

values.text: No mode fault since SPI_SR was last read.
A mode fault occurred since SPI_SR was last read.

fields.name: TDRE
fields.text: Transmit data register empty flag; cleared by writing SPI_TDR, by disabling the SPI, or by reset; set when the SPI is enabled.

values.text: Data written to SPI_TDR has not yet moved to the shift register.
The last data written to SPI_TDR has moved to the shift register.

fields.name: RDRF
fields.text: Receive data register full flag; clears on a read of SPI_RDR.

values.text: Nothing received since SPI_RDR was last read.
Data was received and moved from the shift register to SPI_RDR since SPI_RDR was last read.

registers.name: SPI_IER
registers.title: SPI Interrupt Enable Register
notes: Writable only while WPITEN is 0 in SPI_WPMR.

fields.name: UNDES
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the UNDES interrupt.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the TXEMPTY interrupt.

fields.name: NSSR
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the NSSR interrupt.

fields.name: OVRES
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the OVRES interrupt.

fields.name: MODF
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the MODF interrupt.

fields.name: TDRE
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the TDRE interrupt.

fields.name: RDRF
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the RDRF interrupt.

registers.name: SPI_IDR
registers.title: SPI Interrupt Disable Register
notes: Writable only while WPITEN is 0 in SPI_WPMR.

fields.name: UNDES
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the UNDES interrupt.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the TXEMPTY interrupt.

fields.name: NSSR
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the NSSR interrupt.

fields.name: OVRES
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the OVRES interrupt.

fields.name: MODF
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the MODF interrupt.

fields.name: TDRE
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the TDRE interrupt.

fields.name: RDRF
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the RDRF interrupt.

fields.name: UNDES
fields.text: Reads 1 when the UNDES interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Reads 1 when the TXEMPTY interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: NSSR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the NSSR interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: OVRES
fields.text: Reads 1 when the OVRES interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: MODF
fields.text: Reads 1 when the MODF interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: TDRE
fields.text: Reads 1 when the TDRE interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: RDRF
fields.text: Reads 1 when the RDRF interrupt is enabled.

registers.name: SPI_CSRx
registers.title: SPI Chip Select Register
notes: Writable only while SPI_WPMR.WPEN is 0.
Has to be written even when its reset values are the ones wanted.
BITS takes its translated value only once the register has been written.

fields.name: DLYBCT
fields.text: Delay between two back-to-back transfers to the same peripheral with the chip select held; it follows every transfer and comes before the chip select is released. At 0 there is no delay and the clock keeps its duty cycle across characters; otherwise DLYBCT = delay x fperipheral clock / 32.

fields.name: DLYBS
fields.text: Delay from NPCS falling (going active) to the first valid SPCK edge. At 0 it is half an SPCK period; otherwise DLYBS = delay x fperipheral clock.

fields.name: SCBR
fields.text: Host mode divider from the peripheral clock to the SPCK bit rate, 1 to 255: SCBR = fperipheral clock / SPCK bit rate. 0 is not allowed and starting a transfer with it gives unpredictable results; it resets to 0, so it must be set before the first transfer. If any SPI_CSRx.SCBR used for transfers is 1, every other one used for transfers must be 1 too; unused ones may hold any value.

fields.name: BITS
fields.text: Number of data bits in each transfer; reserved codes must not be used.

fields.name: CSAAT
fields.text: Keeps the chip select active after the last transfer.

values.text: The chip select line goes high right after the final transfer completes.
The chip select line stays active after the last transfer until a transfer is requested on another chip select.

fields.name: CSNAAT
fields.text: Releases the chip select between transfers; ignored when CSAAT = 1.

values.text: The chip select line stays low between two transfers on the same chip select when SPI_TDR is reloaded before the first one ends.
The chip select line rises after every transfer to the same Client and stays inactive for at least DLYBCS / fperipheral clock, with a floor of six periods when DLYBCS is below 6.

fields.name: NCPHA
fields.text: Sets which SPCK edge changes data and which captures it; works with CPOL to give the clock/data relationship between Host and Client.

values.text: Data changes on the leading SPCK edge and is captured on the next.
Data is captured on the leading SPCK edge and changes on the next.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Sets the idle level of SPCK; works with NCPHA to give the clock/data relationship between Host and Client.

fields.name: WPKEY
fields.text: Key that must accompany a write to WPEN.

values.name: PASSWD
values.text: The key; writing any other value cancels the write to WPEN. Reads as 0.

fields.name: WPEN
fields.text: Turns write protection on or off.

values.text: Write protection off, when WPKEY is 0x535049 ("SPI" in ASCII).
Write protection on, when WPKEY is 0x535049 ("SPI" in ASCII).

fields.name: WPVSRC
fields.text: When WPVS = 1, the offset of the register a write was attempted to.

fields.name: WPVS
fields.text: Write protection violation flag.

values.text: No write protection violation since SPI_WPSR was last read.
A write protection violation occurred since SPI_WPSR was last read; an attempted write to a protected register has its offset recorded in WPVSRC.

fields.name: LASTXFER
fields.text: Last transfer: a write of 1 releases chip select once the character in QSPI_TDR.TD has gone out.

values.text: Chip select is released when the character held in QSPI_TDR.TD has finished transferring.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: QSPI software reset; a write of 1 resets the QSPI, and the DMA channels are left untouched.

values.text: Resets the QSPI interface in hardware, triggered from software.

fields.name: QSPIDIS
fields.text: QSPI disable: a write of 1 stops the QSPI after any transfer under way completes, then puts every pin in input mode with nothing sent or received; with QSPIEN and QSPIDIS both written 1 at once, the QSPI ends up disabled.

fields.name: QSPIEN
fields.text: QSPI enable: a write of 1 lets the QSPI send and receive data.

values.text: Turns the QSPI on for transmit and receive.

registers.name: QSPI_MR
registers.title: QSPI Mode Register
notes: Writable only while WPEN is 0 in QSPI_WPMR.

fields.name: DLYCS
fields.text: Shortest time QCS is held inactive between one deactivation and the next activation, which assures the Client its minimum deselect time; 0 inserts one peripheral clock period, otherwise DLYCS = minimum inactive time × fperipheral clock.

fields.name: DLYBCT
fields.text: Delay between two back-to-back transfers to the same peripheral while chip select stays active, inserted after every transfer and ahead of any chip select release; 0 inserts no delay and QSCK keeps its duty cycle across characters, and with SMM = 1 it must be 0; otherwise DLYBCT = (delay × fperipheral clock) / 32.

fields.name: NBBITS
fields.text: Number of bits in each transfer.

fields.name: CSMODE
fields.text: Chip select mode: picks the event that releases chip select; when SMM is 1 this field is held at the LASTXFER setting.

values.name: NOT_RELOADED
values.text: Released when QSPI_TDR.TD is not refilled before the current transfer ends.

values.name: LASTXFER
values.text: Released once LASTXFER is written 1 and the character in QSPI_TDR.TD has gone out.

fields.name: WDRBT
fields.text: Wait data read before transfer: 0 (DISABLED) lets an SPI-mode transfer start whatever QSPI_RDR holds; 1 (ENABLED) holds an SPI-mode transfer until QSPI_RDR has no unread data, so no receive overrun occurs. The QSPI in SPI mode lacks this feature, so WDRBT is to be disregarded.

values.name: DISABLED
values.text: Off; an SPI-mode transfer may start whatever QSPI_RDR holds.

values.name: ENABLED
values.text: An SPI-mode transfer waits until QSPI_RDR holds no unread data.

fields.name: LLB
fields.text: Local loopback enable, for testing in SPI mode only, with MISO tied inside to MOSI at the data serializer: 0 (DISABLED) turns the path off, 1 (ENABLED) turns it on.

fields.name: SMM
fields.text: Serial memory mode: 0 (SPI) runs the QSPI in SPI mode, 1 (MEMORY) in Serial Memory mode.

fields.name: RD
fields.text: Data the QSPI has received, right-aligned; bits not used read as 0.

fields.name: TD
fields.text: Data for the QSPI to send, written right-aligned.

fields.name: QSPIENS
fields.text: QSPI enable status.

fields.name: INSTRE
fields.text: Instruction end flag, cleared when QSPI_SR is read.

values.text: No instruction has ended since QSPI_SR was last read.
One or more instructions have ended since QSPI_SR was last read.

fields.name: CSS
fields.text: Chip select status.

fields.name: CSR
fields.text: Chip select rise flag, cleared when QSPI_SR is read.

values.text: Chip select has not risen since QSPI_SR was last read.
Chip select has risen one or more times since QSPI_SR was last read.

fields.name: OVRES
fields.text: Overrun error flag, cleared when QSPI_SR is read; an overrun is QSPI_RDR being loaded from the serializer two or more times between reads of QSPI_RDR.

values.text: No overrun since QSPI_SR was last read.
One or more overruns since QSPI_SR was last read.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Transmission registers empty flag, cleared by a write to QSPI_TDR.

values.text: Cleared the moment data is written to QSPI_TDR.
QSPI_TDR and the internal shifter hold nothing; with a transfer delay set, the flag rises once that delay has run out.

fields.name: TDRE
fields.text: Transmit data register empty flag, cleared by a write to QSPI_TDR; it reads 0 at reset and while the QSPI is disabled, and the QSPI enable command sets it.

values.text: QSPI_TDR holds written data not yet moved to the serializer.
The last data written to QSPI_TDR has moved to the serializer.

fields.name: RDRF
fields.text: Receive data register full flag, cleared by a read of QSPI_RDR.

values.text: Nothing received since QSPI_RDR was last read.
Data has been received and moved from the serializer into QSPI_RDR since QSPI_RDR was last read.

fields.name: INSTRE
fields.text: Instruction end interrupt enable: a write of 1 enables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CSS
fields.text: Chip select status interrupt enable: a write of 1 enables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CSR
fields.text: Chip select rise interrupt enable: a write of 1 enables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVRES
fields.text: Overrun error interrupt enable: a write of 1 enables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Transmission registers empty interrupt enable: a write of 1 enables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TDRE
fields.text: Transmit data register empty interrupt enable: a write of 1 enables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RDRF
fields.text: Receive data register full interrupt enable: a write of 1 enables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: INSTRE
fields.text: Instruction end interrupt disable: a write of 1 disables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CSS
fields.text: Chip select status interrupt disable: a write of 1 disables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CSR
fields.text: Chip select rise interrupt disable: a write of 1 disables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVRES
fields.text: Overrun error interrupt disable: a write of 1 disables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Transmission registers empty interrupt disable: a write of 1 disables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TDRE
fields.text: Transmit data register empty interrupt disable: a write of 1 disables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RDRF
fields.text: Receive data register full interrupt disable: a write of 1 disables it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: INSTRE
fields.text: Instruction end interrupt mask: reads 1 when the interrupt is enabled, 0 when not.

fields.name: CSS
fields.text: Chip select status interrupt mask: reads 1 when the interrupt is enabled, 0 when not.

fields.name: CSR
fields.text: Chip select rise interrupt mask: reads 1 when the interrupt is enabled, 0 when not.

fields.name: OVRES
fields.text: Overrun error interrupt mask: reads 1 when the interrupt is enabled, 0 when not.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Transmission registers empty interrupt mask: reads 1 when the interrupt is enabled, 0 when not.

fields.name: TDRE
fields.text: Transmit data register empty interrupt mask: reads 1 when the interrupt is enabled, 0 when not.

fields.name: RDRF
fields.text: Receive data register full interrupt mask: reads 1 when the interrupt is enabled, 0 when not.

registers.name: QSPI_SCR
registers.title: QSPI Serial Clock Register
notes: Writable only while WPEN is 0 in QSPI_WPMR.

fields.name: DLYBS
fields.text: Time from QCS going valid to the first valid QSCK edge; 0 gives half a QSCK period, any other value gives DLYBS = delay × fperipheral clock.

fields.name: SCBR
fields.text: Divider, 0 to 255, for the modulus counter that derives QSCK from the peripheral clock: SCBR = (fperipheral clock / QSCK baud rate) - 1.

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: Clock phase: chooses which QSCK edge launches data and which samples it; used together with CPOL to match the Host and Client clock/data timing.

values.text: Data sampled on the leading QSCK edge and changed on the next edge.
Data changed on the leading QSCK edge and sampled on the next edge.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Clock polarity: sets the level QSCK rests at when idle; used together with CPHA to match the Host and Client clock/data timing.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Address sent to the serial Flash memory in the instruction frame.

fields.name: OPT
fields.text: Option code sent to the serial Flash memory.

fields.name: INST
fields.text: Instruction code sent to the serial Flash memory.

fields.name: NBDUM
fields.text: Number of dummy cycles the serial Flash memory needs ahead of the data transfer.

fields.name: CRM
fields.text: Continuous read mode: 0 (DISABLED) turns it off, 1 (ENABLED) turns it on.

fields.name: TFRTYP
fields.text: Type of data transfer.

values.name: TRSFR_READTRSFR_REGISTER
values.text: Read (or read/write) transfer with the serial memory; no scrambling, and no random-location fetch from the serial Flash.

values.name: TRSFR_READ_MEMORYTRSFR_MEMORY
values.text: Read (or read/write) data transfer with the serial memory; scrambled when scrambling is enabled, and random-location fetch from the serial Flash is allowed.

values.name: TRSFR_WRITE
values.text: Write transfer to the serial memory, without scrambling.

values.name: TRSFR_WRITE_MEMORY
values.text: Write data transfer to the serial memory, scrambled when scrambling is enabled.

fields.name: ADDRL
fields.text: Address length: 0 (24_BIT) gives a 24-bit address, 1 (32_BIT) a 32-bit address.

fields.name: OPTL
fields.text: Length of the option code; it has to agree with WIDTH, so a 1-bit option code (OPTL = 0) does not fit WIDTH = 6, where the option code goes out over QuadSPI and needs at least 4 bits.

fields.name: DATAEN
fields.text: Data enable.

values.text: No data goes to or comes from the serial Flash memory.
Data goes to or comes from the serial Flash memory.

fields.name: OPTEN
fields.text: Option enable.

values.text: No option goes to the serial Flash.
The option goes to the serial Flash.

fields.name: ADDREN
fields.text: Address enable.

values.text: No transfer address goes to the serial Flash.
The transfer address goes to the serial Flash.

fields.name: INSTEN
fields.text: Instruction enable.

values.text: No instruction goes to the serial Flash.
The instruction goes to the serial Flash.

fields.name: WIDTH
fields.text: Bus width used for the instruction code, the address and option code, and the data.

values.name: DUAL_OUTPUT
values.text: Instruction and address/option on 1 line; data on 2 lines.

values.name: QUAD_OUTPUT
values.text: Instruction and address/option on 1 line; data on 4 lines.

values.name: DUAL_IO
values.text: Instruction on 1 line; address/option and data on 2 lines.

values.name: QUAD_IO
values.text: Instruction on 1 line; address/option and data on 4 lines.

values.name: DUAL_CMD
values.text: All three phases on 2 lines (dual SPI).

values.name: QUAD_CMD
values.text: All three phases on 4 lines (quad SPI).

registers.name: QSPI_SMR
registers.title: QSPI Scrambling Mode Register
notes: Writable only while WPEN is 0 in QSPI_WPMR.

fields.name: RVDIS
fields.text: Scrambling/unscrambling random value disable.

values.text: Scrambling uses the user key together with a random value that can vary from one device to another.
Scrambling uses the user key alone.

fields.name: SCREN
fields.text: Scrambling/unscrambling enable: 0 (DISABLED) turns it off, 1 (ENABLED) turns it on.

registers.name: QSPI_SKR
registers.title: QSPI Scrambling Key Register
notes: Writable only while WPEN is 0 in QSPI_WPMR.

fields.name: USRK
fields.text: User scrambling key.

fields.name: WPKEY
fields.text: Write protection key; WPEN is written only when this field holds the key.

values.name: PASSWD
values.text: Key 0x515350 ("QSP" in ASCII); a write with any other value is ignored for WPEN, and the field reads 0.

fields.name: WPEN
fields.text: Write protection enable for the QSPI's protectable registers.

values.text: With the key 0x515350 ("QSP" in ASCII) in WPKEY, turns write protection off.
With the key 0x515350 ("QSP" in ASCII) in WPKEY, turns write protection on.

fields.name: WPVSRC
fields.text: Offset of the register a write was attempted on, valid when WPVS = 1.

fields.name: WPVS
fields.text: Write protection violation status.

values.text: No write protection violation since QSPI_WPSR was last read.
A write protection violation has happened since QSPI_WPSR was last read; when it was an attempt to write a protected register, WPVSRC gives that register.

fields.name: FIFODIS
fields.text: FIFO disable.

values.text: Turns the transmit and receive FIFOs off.

fields.name: FIFOEN
fields.text: FIFO enable.

values.text: Turns the transmit and receive FIFOs on.

fields.name: LOCKCLR
fields.text: Lock clear.

fields.name: THRCLR
fields.text: Transmit holding register clear.

values.text: Empties the transmit holding register and sets the TXRDY and TXCOMP flags.

fields.name: ACMDIS
fields.text: Alternative command mode disable.

fields.name: ACMEN
fields.text: Alternative command mode enable.

fields.name: CLEAR
fields.text: Bus clear command.

values.text: In Host mode, sends a bus clear command.

fields.name: PECRQ
fields.text: PEC request.

values.text: Asks for a PEC check or a PEC transmission.

fields.name: PECDIS
fields.text: Packet error checking disable.

values.text: Turns SMBus PEC (CRC) generation and checking off.

fields.name: PECEN
fields.text: Packet error checking enable.

values.text: Turns SMBus PEC (CRC) generation and checking on.

fields.name: SMBDIS
fields.text: SMBus mode disable.

fields.name: SMBEN
fields.text: SMBus mode enable.

values.text: Turns SMBus mode on, provided SMBDIS = 0.

fields.name: HSDIS
fields.text: High-speed mode disable.

fields.name: HSEN
fields.text: High-speed mode enable.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Software reset.

values.text: Has the same effect as a system reset.

fields.name: QUICK
fields.text: SMBus quick command.

values.text: In Host mode, sends an SMBus Quick Command.

fields.name: SVDIS
fields.text: Client mode disable.

values.text: Turns Client mode off; on a read, the characters in the shifter and in the holding register (if it has data) are sent first, and on a write the character under way has to be fully received before disabling.

fields.name: SVEN
fields.text: Client mode enable; changing from Host to Client mode is allowed only while TXCOMP = 1.

values.text: Turns Client mode on; SVDIS must be written 0.

fields.name: MSDIS
fields.text: Host mode disable.

values.text: Turns Host mode off after all pending data has gone out; on a write, the characters in the shifter and in the holding register (if it has data) are sent, and on a read the character under way has to be fully received before disabling.

fields.name: MSEN
fields.text: Host mode enable; changing from Client to Host mode is allowed only while TXCOMP = 1.

values.text: Turns Host mode on; MSDIS must be written 0.

fields.name: STOP
fields.text: Send a STOP condition.

values.text: Sends STOP right after the byte now being sent in Host Read mode; a single-byte Host read sets START and STOP together, a multi-byte Host read sets STOP after the next-to-last byte is received, a NACK received in Host Read mode brings an automatic STOP, and in a Host write STOP follows once the current data has gone out.

fields.name: START
fields.text: Send a START condition; needed for the TWIHS to read from a Client, while in Host mode a write frame goes out as soon as a character is written to TWIHS_THR.

values.text: Sends a frame that starts with a START bit, set up as TWIHS_MMR defines.

fields.name: DADR
fields.text: Address of the Client device to read or write; used in Host mode only.

fields.name: MREAD
fields.text: Host read direction.

fields.name: IADRSZ
fields.text: Size of the internal device address.

fields.name: DATAMEN
fields.text: Data matching enable.

values.text: Matching on the first received data is off.
Matching on the first received data is on.

fields.name: SADR3EN
fields.text: Client address 3 enable.

values.text: Matching on Client address 3 is off.
Matching on Client address 3 is on.

fields.name: SADR2EN
fields.text: Client address 2 enable.

values.text: Matching on Client address 2 is off.
Matching on Client address 2 is on.

fields.name: SADR1EN
fields.text: Client address 1 enable.

values.text: Matching on Client address 1 is off.
Matching on Client address 1 is on.

fields.name: SADR
fields.text: Address the TWIHS answers to in Client mode when a Host reads or writes it; it must be set before Client mode is enabled or after a general call, and writes at any other time do nothing.

fields.name: MASK
fields.text: Mask on the Client address in Client mode, so several addresses are answered: each MASK bit at 1 masks the matching SADR bit, and MASK = 0 masks nothing.

fields.name: SCLWSDIS
fields.text: Clock wait state disable.

values.text: In Client mode the clock is never stretched, and OVRE and UNRE report overrun and underrun.

fields.name: SMHH
fields.text: SMBus host header.

values.text: The SMBus host header is not acknowledged.
The SMBus host header is acknowledged.

fields.name: SMDA
fields.text: SMBus default address.

values.text: The SMBus default address is not acknowledged.
The SMBus default address is acknowledged.

fields.name: NACKEN
fields.text: Client receiver data phase NACK enable.

values.text: The normal value is returned in the data-phase ACK cycle in Client Receiver mode.
A NACK is returned in the data-phase ACK cycle in Client Receiver mode.

fields.name: IADR
fields.text: Internal address: 0, 1, 2 or 3 bytes, as IADRSZ sets.

registers.name: TWIHS_CWGR
registers.title: TWIHS Clock Waveform Generator Register
notes: Writable only while WPEN is 0 in TWIHS_WPMR.
Used in Host mode only.

fields.name: HOLD
fields.text: TWD hold time after TWCK falls: in High-speed mode TWD is adjusted internally at that edge so the I2C maximum hold time is met; otherwise TWD stays put for (HOLD + 3) × tperipheral clock after it.

fields.name: CKDIV

values.text: Turns the transmitter off; I2SC_SR.TXEN clears once it has stopped.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: Transmitter enable.

values.text: Turns the transmitter on unless TXDIS is 1; I2SC_SR.TXEN sets once it has started.

fields.name: CKDIS
fields.text: Clocks disable.

fields.name: CKEN
fields.text: Clocks enable.

values.text: Starts I2SC clock generation unless CKDIS is 1.

fields.name: RXDIS
fields.text: Receiver disable.

values.text: Turns the receiver off; I2SC_SR.RXEN clears once it has stopped.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: Receiver enable.

values.text: Turns the receiver on unless RXDIS is 1; I2SC_SR.RXEN sets once it is running.

fields.name: IWS
fields.text: Width of the I2SC_WS slot for 18-, 20- and 24-bit data.

values.text: 32-bit slot for DATALENGTH of 18, 20 or 24 bits.
24-bit slot for DATALENGTH of 18, 20 or 24 bits.

fields.name: IMCKMODE
fields.text: Host clock mode; must be 0 when I2SC_MCK runs at the I2SC_CK frequency.

values.text: No host clock; the selected clock drives I2SC_CK.
Host clock made; the internally generated clock goes out on I2SC_MCK.

fields.name: IMCKFS
fields.text: Host clock to sample rate ratio: the host clock runs at [2 x 16 x (IMCKFS + 1)] / (IMCKDIV + 1) times the I2SC_WS frequency.

fields.name: IMCKDIV
fields.text: Divider from the selected clock to the I2SC_MCK host clock, which runs at the selected clock over (IMCKDIV + 1); works with IMCKFS. Write-only, reads 0; never write 0.

fields.name: TXSAME
fields.text: What the transmitter sends on underrun.

fields.name: TXDMA
fields.text: Single or multiple DMA Controller channels for the transmitter.

values.text: One DMA Controller channel serves all audio channels.
One DMA Controller channel per audio channel.

fields.name: TXMONO
fields.text: Transmit mono.

values.text: Mono: the I2SC copies each left sample to the right channel.

fields.name: RXLOOP
fields.text: Loopback test mode.

values.text: I2SC_DO is tied internally to I2SC_DI.

fields.name: RXDMA
fields.text: Single or multiple DMA Controller channels for the receiver.

values.text: One DMA Controller channel serves all audio channels.
One DMA Controller channel per audio channel.

fields.name: RXMONO
fields.text: Receive mono.

values.text: Mono: the I2SC copies each left sample to the right channel.

fields.name: DATALENGTH
fields.text: Data word length.

values.name: 16_BITS_COMPACT
values.text: 16-bit compact stereo: left sample in bits 15:0, right in bits 31:16 of one word.

values.name: 8_BITS_COMPACT
values.text: 8-bit compact stereo: left sample in bits 7:0, right in bits 15:8 of one word.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Inter-IC sound controller mode.

values.name: Client
values.text: Bit clock and word select/frame sync come in on the I2SC_CK and I2SC_WS pins.

values.name: Host
values.text: The I2SC makes bit clock and word select/frame sync from MCK and drives them on I2SC_CK and I2SC_WS; with IMCKMODE set, the peripheral clock or GCLK goes out on I2SC_MCK as host clock.

fields.name: TXURCH
fields.text: Transmit underrun per channel: bit i sets when channel i (0 is the first in the frame) underruns; the field clears when I2SC_SCR.TXUR is written 1.

values.text: Bit i sets on a transmit underrun in channel i, channel 0 being the first of the frame.

fields.name: RXORCH
fields.text: Receive overrun per channel: bit i sets when channel i (0 is the first in the frame) overruns; the field clears when I2SC_SCR.RXOR is written 1.

fields.name: TXUR
fields.text: Transmit underrun flag.

values.text: Cleared by writing 1 to the matching I2SC_SCR bit.
Set by an underrun on I2SC_THR or by writing 1 to the matching I2SC_SSR bit.

fields.name: TXRDY
fields.text: Transmit ready flag.

values.text: Cleared by a write to I2SC_THR.
I2SC_THR is empty and takes new data to send.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: Transmitter enabled status.

values.text: Clears when the transmitter is turned off by I2SC_CR.TXDIS or I2SC_CR.SWRST.
Sets when the transmitter is turned on by I2SC_CR.TXEN.

fields.name: RXOR
fields.text: Receive overrun flag.

values.text: Cleared by writing 1 to the matching I2SC_SCR bit.
Set by an overrun on I2SC_RHR or by writing 1 to the matching I2SC_SSR bit.

fields.name: RXRDY
fields.text: Receive ready flag.

values.text: Received data is waiting in I2SC_RHR.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: Receiver enabled status.

values.text: Clears when the receiver is turned off by I2SC_CR.RXDIS or SWRST.
Sets when the receiver is turned on by I2SC_CR.RXEN.

fields.name: RHR
fields.text: Last data word received, written by hardware; right-justified when I2SC_MR.DATALENGTH is under 32 bits.

fields.name: THR
fields.text: Data word to send after the current one, when TXRDY is not set; right-justified when I2SC_MR.DATALENGTH is under 32 bits.

fields.name: LINWKUP
fields.text: Writing 1 puts a wakeup signal out on the LIN bus.

fields.name: LINABT
fields.text: Writing 1 aborts the LIN transmission in progress.

values.text: Abort the LIN transmission under way.

fields.name: RTSDIS
fields.text: Writing 1 drives the RTS pin: to 0 when US_MR.USART_MODE is 2, to 1 when it is 0.

values.text: RTS pin driven to 0 with USART_MODE = 2, or to 1 with USART_MODE = 0.

fields.name: RTSEN
fields.text: Writing 1 drives the RTS pin: to 1 when US_MR.USART_MODE is 2, to 0 when it is 0.

values.text: RTS pin driven to 1 with USART_MODE = 2, or to 0 with USART_MODE = 0.

fields.name: DTRDIS
fields.text: Writing 1 drives the DTR pin high.

fields.name: DTREN
fields.text: Writing 1 drives the DTR pin low.

fields.name: RETTO
fields.text: Writing 1 restarts the timeout period at once.

fields.name: RSTNACK
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the NACK flag in US_CSR.

fields.name: RSTIT
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the ITER flag in US_CSR; does nothing unless ISO7816 is enabled.

values.text: US_CSR.ITER cleared, only with ISO7816 enabled.

fields.name: SENDA
fields.text: Writing 1 in Multidrop mode makes the next character written to US_THR go out with its address bit set.

values.text: Next US_THR character sent with the address bit set (Multidrop mode only).

fields.name: STTTO
fields.text: Writing 1 clears US_CSR.TIMEOUT, stops any running timeout period and holds the timeout counter until a character arrives.

values.text: Clear TIMEOUT, cancel the current period and arm the counter on the next received character.

fields.name: STPBRK
fields.text: Writing 1 ends a break being sent: the line goes high for 12 bit periods once the break has lasted at least one character time; nothing happens when no break is on.

values.text: End the break after at least one character time, then hold the line high for 12 bit periods.

fields.name: STTBRK
fields.text: Writing 1 starts a break once both US_THR and the shift register have emptied; nothing happens when a break is already on.

values.text: Begin a break after pending characters have gone out.

fields.name: RSTSTA
fields.text: Writing 1 clears these US_CSR flags: PARE, FRAME, OVRE, RXBRK, MANERR, and the LIN flags LINBK, LINID, LINTC, LINBE, LINCE, LINIPE, LINISFE, LINSNRE, LINSTE, LINHTE.

fields.name: TXDIS
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the transmitter off.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the transmitter on, as long as TXDIS is 0.

fields.name: RXDIS
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the receiver off.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: Writing 1 turns the receiver on, as long as RXDIS is 0.

fields.name: RSTTX
fields.text: Writing 1 resets the transmitter.

fields.name: RSTRX
fields.text: Writing 1 resets the receiver.

notes: Applies only when US_MR.USART_MODE is 0xE or 0xF.

fields.name: RCS
fields.text: In SPI Host mode (USART_MODE = 0xE), writing 1 releases the NSS client select line on the RTS pin.

fields.name: FCS
fields.text: In SPI Host mode (USART_MODE = 0xE), writing 1 holds the NSS client select line (RTS pin) at 0 even while nothing is sent, for SPI clients using CSAAT (chip select active after transfer).

values.text: NSS (RTS pin) forced to 0 regardless of transmission.

fields.name: RSTSTA
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the OVRE and UNRE flags of US_CSR.

fields.name: RSTTX

registers.name: US_MR
registers.title: USART Mode Register
notes: Writable only while WPEN is 0 in US_WPMR.

fields.name: ONEBIT
fields.text: Picks the start frame delimiter: COMMAND or DATA SYNC, or a single bit.

fields.name: MODSYNC
fields.text: Sets the direction of the Manchester start bit transition.

fields.name: MAN
fields.text: Turns the Manchester encoder and decoder on.

fields.name: FILTER
fields.text: Turns on a filter on the receive line.

values.text: Receive line filtered by a three-sample, 2-of-3 majority filter at the 1/16-bit clock.

fields.name: MAX_ITERATION
fields.text: Maximum number of automatic repetitions in ISO7816 mode, protocol T = 0.

fields.name: INVDATA
fields.text: Inverts the voltage polarity of the data field on TXD and of what US_RHR returns from RXD or the ISO7816 IO line; used together with MSBF.

values.text: Normal: TXD carries US_THR as written, US_RHR matches the line.
Inverted: TXD and US_RHR data are the inverse of US_THR and of the received line; suited to contactless cards, used with MSBF.

fields.name: VAR_SYNC
fields.text: Chooses where the command/data sync field comes from.

values.text: Sync field set by the user through MODSYNC.
Sync field taken from each character written to US_THR.

fields.name: DSNACK
fields.text: Limits the NACKs sent on successive parity errors; MAX_ITERATION must be 0 while DSNACK is 0.

values.text: A NACK goes out on the ISO line at each parity error, unless INACK is set.
Parity errors in a row are counted up to MAX_ITERATION, each sending a NACK; at the limit NACKs stop and ITER is set.

fields.name: INACK
fields.text: Stops the USART from generating NACK.

fields.name: OVER
fields.text: Selects the oversampling rate.

fields.name: CLKO
fields.text: Lets the USART drive the SCK pin, unless USCLKS selects SCK as the external clock.

values.text: SCK pin driven, when USCLKS does not select external SCK.

fields.name: MODE9
fields.text: Selects 9-bit characters in place of the CHRL length.

fields.name: MSBF
fields.text: Selects which bit goes on the line first.

fields.name: CHMODE
fields.text: Selects normal operation or a test loop.

values.name: AUTOMATIC
values.text: Automatic echo: receiver input tied to the TXD pin.

values.name: LOCAL_LOOPBACK
values.text: Local loopback: transmitter output tied to the receiver input.

values.name: REMOTE_LOOPBACK
values.text: Remote loopback: RXD pin tied internally to TXD pin.

fields.name: NBSTOP

fields.text: Selects synchronous or asynchronous operation.

Re-arms the comparison trigger so the receive holding register can load.

fields.name: RSTSTA
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the PARE, FRAME, CMP and OVRE flags in UART_SR.

fields.text: Writing 1 turns the transmitter off; unless RSTTX is also set, a character in progress and one waiting in UART_THR are both sent first.

values.text: Transmitter off, after finishing any character in progress and one held in UART_THR, unless RSTTX is set.

fields.text: Writing 1 turns the transmitter on, provided TXDIS is 0.

fields.name: RXDIS

fields.name: TXRDY

fields.name: RXRDY

fields.text: Writing 1 disables the comparison interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the TXEMPTY interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: PARE

fields.name: FRAME
fields.text: Writing 1 disables the framing error interrupt; 0 has no effect.

fields.name: OVRE
