fields.text: Reads 1 when the comparison interrupt is enabled, 0 when it is disabled.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Reads 1 when the TXEMPTY interrupt is enabled, 0 when it is disabled.

fields.name: PARE
fields.text: Reads 1 when the parity error interrupt is enabled, 0 when it is disabled.

fields.name: FRAME
fields.text: Reads 1 when the framing error interrupt is enabled, 0 when it is disabled.

fields.name: OVRE
fields.text: Reads 1 when the overrun error interrupt is enabled, 0 when it is disabled.

fields.name: TXRDY
fields.text: Reads 1 when the TXRDY interrupt is enabled, 0 when it is disabled.

fields.name: RXRDY
fields.text: Reads 1 when the RXRDY interrupt is enabled, 0 when it is disabled.

fields.name: CMP
fields.text: Set when a received character meets the comparison set by VAL1, VAL2 and CMPPAR; cleared by RSTSTA.

values.text: No matching character since the last RSTSTA.
A received character matched the comparison.

fields.name: TXEMPTY
fields.text: Shows whether the transmitter has nothing left to send, neither in UART_THR nor in progress.

values.text: Characters remain in UART_THR or in the transmitter, or the transmitter is off.
UART_THR is empty and the transmitter is idle.

fields.name: PARE
fields.text: Set on a parity error; cleared by RSTSTA.

values.text: No parity error since the last RSTSTA.
One or more parity errors since the last RSTSTA.

fields.name: FRAME
fields.text: Set on a framing error; cleared by RSTSTA.

values.text: No framing error since the last RSTSTA.
One or more framing errors since the last RSTSTA.

fields.name: OVRE
fields.text: Set on an overrun; cleared by RSTSTA.

values.text: No overrun since the last RSTSTA.
One or more overruns since the last RSTSTA.

fields.name: TXRDY
fields.text: Shows whether UART_THR can take a new character.

values.text: UART_THR holds a character not yet moved to the shift register, or the transmitter is off.
No character waits in UART_THR for the shift register.

fields.name: RXRDY
fields.text: Shows whether a received character is waiting in UART_RHR.

values.text: Nothing received since UART_RHR was last read, or the receiver is off.
A complete character sits unread in UART_RHR.

fields.name: RXCHR
fields.text: The most recent received character, valid when RXRDY is set.

fields.name: TXCHR
fields.text: The character to send next, after the current one when TXRDY is not set.

fields.name: CD
fields.text: Divides the baud clock source: baud rate = source / (16 x CD), the source being the peripheral clock when BRSRCCK = 0 or PCKx when BRSRCCK = 1; 0 stops the baud rate clock.

values.text: CD = f(peripheral clock) / (16 x baud rate) when BRSRCCK = 0, or f(PCKx) / (16 x baud rate) when BRSRCCK = 1; values 1 to 65,535.
With BRSRCCK = 0: CD = f(peripheral clock) / (16 x baud rate).
With BRSRCCK = 1: CD = f(PCKx) / (16 x baud rate).

fields.name: VAL2
fields.text: Upper bound of the comparison: CMP in UART_SR is set when a received character lies between VAL1 and VAL2 inclusive.

values.text: CMP is set for a character from VAL1 up to VAL2 inclusive; with SleepWalking enabled in PMC_SLPWK_ER, a match also requests a system wake-up.

fields.name: CMPPAR
fields.text: Chooses whether the parity bit counts in the comparison.

values.text: Parity ignored; a parity error does not stop a wake-up.
Parity checked; a parity error voids a data match and no wake-up occurs.

fields.name: CMPMODE
fields.text: Chooses whether reception waits for a comparison match.

values.name: FLAG_ONLY
values.text: Every character is received; the comparison only drives CMP.

values.name: START_CONDITION
values.text: Reception starts only once the comparison is met.

fields.name: VAL1
fields.text: Lower bound of the comparison: CMP in UART_SR is set when a received character lies between VAL1 and VAL2 inclusive.

values.text: CMP is set for a character from VAL1 up to VAL2 inclusive; with SleepWalking enabled in PMC_SLPWK_ER, a match also requests a system wake-up.

fields.name: WPKEY
fields.text: Key that must accompany a write to WPEN; reads 0.

values.name: PASSWD
values.text: The only accepted key; any other value cancels the write.

fields.name: WPEN
fields.text: Turns on write protection of the UART's protectable registers.

values.text: Write protection off, when WPKEY is 0x554152.
Write protection on, when WPKEY is 0x554152.

fields.name: FCNT
fields.text: Sets how many frames make up one sub-buffer on synchronous channels.

fields.name: CTLRETRY
fields.text: Chooses whether a control packet the receiver answers with Break or ProtocolError is sent again.

fields.name: ASYRETRY
fields.text: Chooses whether an asynchronous packet the receiver answers with Break or ProtocolError is sent again.

fields.name: ZERO

fields.text: When 1, asynchronous Tx channels set their bit in MLB_MS0 or MLB_MS1 on a packet sent without error.

fields.text: When 1, asynchronous Rx channels set their bit in MLB_MS0 or MLB_MS1 on a packet received without error.

fields.text: One bit per channel 0 to 31; a 1 marks that channel busy.

fields.name: CHB
fields.text: One bit per channel 32 to 63; a 1 marks that channel busy.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Bits 31:0 of a 128-bit CTR entry, or an 8-bit DBR entry in bits 7:0.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Bits 63:32 of a 128-bit CTR entry.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Bits 95:64 of a 128-bit CTR entry.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Bits 127:96 of a 128-bit CTR entry.

fields.name: MASK
fields.text: Write enables for CTR data bits 63:32; a 1 in bit n enables that CTR data bit.

fields.text: Write enables for CTR data bits 95:64; a 1 in bit n enables that CTR data bit.

fields.text: Selects DMA mode 0 or 1.

fields.text: Chooses whether both channel status registers share one interrupt line.

values.text: MLB_ACSR0 drives MediaLB IRQ0 and MLB_ACSR1 drives MediaLB IRQ1.
MLB_ACSR0 and MLB_ACSR1 both drive MediaLB IRQ0.

fields.text: Chooses how channel interrupt bits are cleared.

registers.name: MLB_ACSR0

notes: Each of the 64 physical channels has a bit across MLB_ACSR0 and MLB_ACSR1, set when DNEn or ERRn is set in that channel's AHB channel descriptor, and signalled to the host controller on ahb_int[1:0]. A bit in MLB_ACSR0 (channels 31 to 0) raises MediaLB IRQ0; a bit in MLB_ACSR1 (channels 63 to 32) raises MediaLB IRQ1, or IRQ0 when MLB_ACTL.SMX = 1. With MLB_ACTL.SCE = 0, reading the register clears its bits; with SCE = 1, software writes 1 to each bit to clear it.

fields.name: CHS

fields.name: CHS
fields.text: One bit per channel 32 to 63; a 1 means that channel has an interrupt pending; cleared by writing 1 when MLB_ACTL.SCE = 1, or by reading the register when SCE = 0.

fields.name: CHM

fields.text: Core release number, one BCD digit.

fields.name: STEP
fields.text: Step within the core release, one BCD digit.

fields.name: SUBSTEP
fields.text: Sub-step within the core release, one BCD digit.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Year of the timestamp, one BCD digit, fixed when the MCAN was synthesised.

fields.name: MON
fields.text: Month of the timestamp, two BCD digits, fixed when the MCAN was synthesised.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Day of the timestamp, two BCD digits, fixed when the MCAN was synthesised.

fields.name: ETV
fields.text: Reads 0x87654321, for checking byte order.

fields.name: CSV
fields.text: Value specific to the customer.

registers.name: MCAN_DBTP
registers.title: MCAN Data Bit Timing and Prescaler Register
notes: Writes take effect only with both CCE and INIT set to 1 in MCAN_CCCR.
The bit time spans 4 to 25 time quanta, and the time quantum 1 to 32 CAN core clock periods: tq = (DBRP + 1) core clock periods.
DTSEG1 covers Prop_Seg plus Phase_Seg1 and DTSEG2 covers Phase_Seg2, so a bit lasts (DTSEG1 + DTSEG2 + 3) tq, i.e. Sync_Seg + Prop_Seg + Phase_Seg1 + Phase_Seg2.
The Information Processing Time is zero: the next bit's data is available on the clock edge right after the sample point.
With an 8 MHz CAN core clock, the reset value 0x00000A33 gives a fast bit rate of 500 kbit/s.
The CAN FD data-phase bit rate set here must be no lower than the arbitration-phase bit rate set in MCAN_NBTP.

fields.name: TDC
fields.text: Turns transmitter delay compensation on: 0 = off (DISABLED), 1 = on (ENABLED).

fields.name: DBRP
fields.text: Divider, 0 to 31, applied to the peripheral clock to make the data-phase time quantum; the hardware divides by this value plus one, and the bit time is a whole number of these quanta.

fields.name: DTSEG1
fields.text: Data-phase segment ahead of the sample point, 1 to 31; it lasts tq x (DTSEG1 + 1).

fields.name: DTSEG2
fields.text: Data-phase segment after the sample point; it lasts tq x (DTSEG2 + 1).

fields.name: DSJW
fields.text: Data-phase resynchronization jump width; a jump lasts tq x (DSJW + 1).

registers.name: MCAN_TEST
registers.title: MCAN Test Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000000.
Writable only while MCAN_CCCR.TEST is 1; clearing MCAN_CCCR.TEST puts every MCAN_TEST function back to its reset value.
Loop Back mode and software control of CANTX are hardware test modes; a TX value other than 0 disturbs message transfer on the CAN bus.

fields.name: RX
fields.text: Read-only state of the CANRX pin; undefined after reset.

fields.name: TX
fields.text: Read/write control of the CANTX pin.

values.name: RESET
values.text: Reset value: the CAN core drives CANTX, changing at the end of each bit time.

fields.name: LBCK
fields.text: Read/write Loop Back mode: 0 = off, the reset value (DISABLED); 1 = on (ENABLED).

values.name: DISABLED
values.text: Loop Back off; the reset value.

registers.name: MCAN_RWD
registers.title: MCAN RAM Watchdog Register
notes: The RAM watchdog times the Message RAM's responses: each Message RAM access through the MCAN's Generic Host Interface starts the watchdog counter from MCAN_RWD.WDC, and the Message RAM's READY output, on completing the access, reloads it with MCAN_RWD.WDC.
If the counter counts down to zero before the Message RAM responds, it stops and MCAN_IR.WDI is set.
The counter runs on the peripheral clock (system bus clock).

fields.name: WDV
fields.text: Read-only count of the Message RAM watchdog for the message now in RAM.

fields.name: WDC
fields.text: Read/write value the Message RAM watchdog counter starts from; 0 turns the counter off.

fields.name: NISO
fields.text: Selects the CAN FD frame format; when set, the Bosch CAN FD Specification V1.0 format is used.

values.text: ISO 11898-1 CAN FD format, the default.
Bosch CAN FD Specification V1.0 format.

fields.name: TXP
fields.text: Write-protected. When set, after sending a frame successfully the MCAN waits two CAN bit times before it starts its next transmission.

fields.name: EFBI
fields.text: Write-protected. Edge filtering while integrating into the bus.

values.text: On: a hard-synchronization edge needs two dominant tq in a row.

fields.name: PXHD
fields.text: Write-protected. Handling of protocol exception events.

fields.name: BRSE
fields.text: Write-protected. Bit rate switching on transmit: 0 = off (DISABLED), 1 = on (ENABLED).

values.name: DISABLED
values.text: No bit rate switch when transmitting.

fields.name: FDOE
fields.text: Write-protected. CAN FD operation: 0 = off (DISABLED), 1 = on (ENABLED).

fields.name: TEST
fields.text: Test mode, write-protected against setting: 0 = normal operation with MCAN_TEST at its reset values (DISABLED); 1 = test mode, MCAN_TEST writable (ENABLED).

values.name: DISABLED
values.text: Normal operation; MCAN_TEST stays at reset values.

values.name: ENABLED
values.text: Test mode; MCAN_TEST can be written.

fields.name: DAR
fields.text: Write-protected. Automatic retransmission of messages that failed to send: 0 = retransmit (AUTO_RETX); 1 = no retransmission (NO_AUTO_RETX).

values.name: AUTO_RETX
values.text: Failed messages are sent again automatically.

fields.name: MON
fields.text: Bus Monitoring mode, write-protected against setting: 0 = off (DISABLED), 1 = on (ENABLED).

fields.name: CSR
fields.text: Asks for the clock to stop: 0 = no request (NO_CLOCK_STOP); 1 = request (CLOCK_STOP), after which INIT and then CSA get set once all pending transfers are done and the bus is idle.

values.name: CLOCK_STOP
values.text: Clock stop requested; INIT, then CSA, go to 1 once pending transfers finish and the bus is idle.

fields.name: CSA
fields.text: Read-only acknowledge of a clock stop request.

values.text: The MCAN may be powered down by stopping both its peripheral clock and its CAN core clock.

fields.name: ASM
fields.text: Restricted Operation mode, write-protected against setting: 0 = normal CAN operation (NORMAL); 1 = Restricted Operation mode active (RESTRICTED).

fields.name: CCE
fields.text: Write-protected. Write access to the protected configuration registers: 0 = none (PROTECTED); 1 = allowed while MCAN_CCCR.INIT = 1 (CONFIGURABLE).

values.name: PROTECTED
values.text: Protected configuration registers cannot be written.

values.name: CONFIGURABLE
values.text: Protected configuration registers can be written while MCAN_CCCR.INIT = 1.

fields.name: INIT
fields.text: Starts initialization: 0 = normal operation (DISABLED), 1 = initialization (ENABLED). A written value takes time to cross clock domains before it reads back, so read INIT back to confirm the last write before writing a new value.

registers.name: MCAN_NBTP
registers.title: MCAN Nominal Bit Timing and Prescaler Register
notes: Writes take effect only with both CCE and INIT set to 1 in MCAN_CCCR.
The bit time spans 4 to 385 time quanta, and the time quantum 1 to 512 CAN core clock periods: tq = t(core clock) x (NBRP + 1).
NTSEG1 covers Prop_Seg plus Phase_Seg1 and NTSEG2 covers Phase_Seg2, so a bit lasts (NTSEG1 + NTSEG2 + 3) tq, i.e. Sync_Seg + Prop_Seg + Phase_Seg1 + Phase_Seg2.
The Information Processing Time is zero: the next bit's data is available on the clock edge right after the sample point.
With an 8 MHz CAN core clock, the reset value 0x06000A03 gives a bit rate of 500 kbit/s.

fields.name: NSJW
fields.text: Nominal resynchronization jump width, 0 to 127; a jump lasts tq x (NSJW + 1).

fields.name: NBRP
fields.text: Nominal prescaler, 0 to 511, dividing the oscillator frequency to make the time quantum: tq = (NBRP + 1) core clock periods; CAN time is a whole number of quanta.

fields.name: NTSEG1
fields.text: Nominal segment ahead of the sample point; it lasts tq x (NTSEG1 + 1).

fields.name: NTSEG2
fields.text: Nominal segment after the sample point; it lasts tq x (NTSEG2 + 1).

registers.name: MCAN_TSCC
registers.title: MCAN Timestamp Counter Configuration Register
notes: CAN FD needs the external counter for timestamps (TSS = 2).

fields.name: TCP
fields.text: Time unit of the timestamp and timeout counters, in CAN bit times from 1 to 16; the hardware uses this value plus one.

fields.name: TSS
fields.text: Source of the timestamp counter value.

values.name: TCP_INC
values.text: Counter counts at the rate set by TCP.

values.name: EXT_TIMESTAMP
values.text: Value taken from an external timestamp counter.

fields.name: TSC
fields.text: Timestamp counter, internal or external, captured at each start of frame on receive and transmit. With MCAN_TSCC.TSS = 1 it counts in steps of 1 to 16 CAN bit times set by MCAN_TSCC.TCP, a write clears it to zero, and a wrap around sets MCAN_IR.TSW; a wrap around means the count going from non-zero to zero other than by a write to MCAN_TSCV. With MCAN_TSCC.TSS = 2 it shows the external counter and a write does nothing.

registers.name: MCAN_TOCC
registers.title: MCAN Timeout Counter Configuration Register
notes: Writes take effect only with both CCE and INIT set to 1 in MCAN_CCCR.

fields.name: TOP
fields.text: Timeout period: the value the down-counting Timeout Counter starts from.

fields.name: TOS
fields.text: Chooses what controls the Timeout Counter. Under Continuous operation, writing MCAN_TOCV reloads it with MCAN_TOCC.TOP and it keeps counting down. Under FIFO control an empty FIFO reloads it with MCAN_TOCC.TOP, and counting down starts when the first element is stored.

fields.name: ETOC
fields.text: Turns the Timeout Counter on: 0 = off (NO_TIMEOUT); 1 = on, controlled by TOS (TOS_CONTROLLED).

fields.name: TOC
fields.text: Timeout counter, counting down in steps of 1 to 16 CAN bit times set by MCAN_TSCC.TCP. On reaching zero it stops and sets MCAN_IR.TOO. MCAN_TOCC.TOS sets how it starts and restarts. A write clears it.

registers.name: MCAN_ECR
registers.title: MCAN Error Counter Register
notes: While MCAN_CCCR.ASM is 1, CAN protocol errors no longer raise TEC or REC, but CEL still counts them.

fields.name: CEL
fields.text: Counts each CAN protocol error that raises the transmit or receive error counter; a read of CEL clears it. It holds at 0xFF, and the next rise of TEC or REC sets IR.ELO.

fields.name: RP
fields.text: Receive error passive state.

values.text: Receive error count under the error passive level of 128.
Receive error count has reached the error passive level of 128.

fields.name: REC
fields.text: Present receive error count, 0 to 127.

fields.name: TEC
fields.text: Present transmit error count, 0 to 255.

fields.name: TDCV
fields.text: Secondary sample point position, 0 to 127 CAN core clock periods: the measured CANTX-to-CANRX delay plus MCAN_TDCR.TDCO.

fields.name: PXE
fields.text: Protocol exception event flag; a read clears it.

fields.name: RFDF
fields.text: Set on receiving a CAN FD message, whether or not acceptance filtering passes it; a read clears it.

values.text: No CAN FD message received since the CPU cleared this bit.
A CAN FD format message with FDF set was received.

fields.name: RBRS
fields.text: BRS flag of the last CAN FD message received; set along with RFDF regardless of acceptance filtering; a read clears it.

values.text: BRS was clear in the last CAN FD message received.
BRS was set in the last CAN FD message received.

fields.name: RESI
fields.text: ESI flag of the last CAN FD message received; set along with RFDF regardless of acceptance filtering; a read clears it.

values.text: ESI was clear in the last CAN FD message received.
ESI was set in the last CAN FD message received.

fields.name: DLEC
fields.text: Kind of the last error seen while a CAN FD format frame with BRS set was in its data phase, coded as LEC. Cleared to zero when such a frame is sent or received without error; a read sets it to 111.

fields.name: BO
fields.text: Bus_Off state.

fields.name: EW
fields.text: Error warning state.

values.text: Both error counters under the Error_Warning limit of 96.
One or both error counters at the Error_Warning limit of 96.

fields.name: EP
fields.text: Error passive state.

values.text: Error_Active: takes part in bus traffic normally and sends an active error flag on detecting an error.

fields.name: ACT
fields.text: State of CAN communication for the module.

fields.name: LEC
fields.text: Kind of the last error seen on the CAN bus; cleared when a message is sent or received without error; a read sets it to 111.

values.name: NO_ERROR
values.text: No error since a successful transfer cleared LEC.

values.name: STUFF_ERROR
values.text: Over 5 equal bits in a row where that is not allowed in a received message.

values.name: FORM_ERROR
values.text: Form error: a received frame had a wrongly formed fixed-format part.

values.name: ACK_ERROR
values.text: No other node acknowledged a message the MCAN sent.

values.name: BIT1_ERROR
values.text: While sending, outside the arbitration field, the MCAN sent recessive (1) but saw dominant on the bus.

values.name: BIT0_ERROR
values.text: While sending a message, acknowledge bit, active error flag or overload flag, the MCAN sent dominant (0) but saw recessive on the bus. During Bus_Off recovery this code is set after each run of 11 recessive bits, so the processor can follow the recovery and see the bus is not stuck dominant or constantly disturbed.

values.name: CRC_ERROR
values.text: Received CRC did not match the CRC computed from the received data.

values.name: NO_CHANGE
values.text: No CAN bus event since the last processor read of MCAN_PSR; every read of MCAN_PSR sets LEC to 7.

fields.name: TDCO
fields.text: Offset, 0 to 127 CAN core clock periods, from the measured CANTX-to-CANRX delay to the secondary sample point.

fields.name: TDCF
fields.text: Earliest allowed secondary sample point position, 0 to 127 CAN core clock periods; dominant CANRX edges that would place it earlier are left out of the delay measurement. Active when TDCF is set above TDCO.

registers.name: MCAN_IR
registers.title: MCAN Interrupt Register
notes: Each flag sets when its condition is detected (edge-sensitive) and stays set until the processor clears it: writing 1 to the bit clears it, writing 0 does nothing. A hard reset clears the register.
MCAN_IE decides whether a flag raises an interrupt, and MCAN_ILS which interrupt line carries it.

fields.name: ARA
fields.text: Interrupt flag: access to a reserved address.

values.text: No access to a reserved address.

fields.name: PED
fields.text: Interrupt flag: protocol error in the data phase.

values.text: Data-phase protocol error seen: MCAN_PSR.DLEC is neither 0 nor 7.

fields.name: PEA
fields.text: Interrupt flag: protocol error in the arbitration phase.

values.text: Arbitration-phase protocol error seen: MCAN_PSR.LEC is neither 0 nor 7.

fields.name: WDI
fields.text: Interrupt flag: message RAM watchdog event.

values.text: Message RAM watchdog event from a missing READY.

fields.name: BO
fields.text: Interrupt flag: change of Bus_Off state.

fields.name: EW
fields.text: Interrupt flag: change of Error_Warning state.

fields.name: EP
fields.text: Interrupt flag: change of Error_Passive state.

fields.name: ELO
fields.text: Interrupt flag: overflow of the CAN error logging counter.

values.text: The CAN error logging counter overflowed.

fields.name: DRX
fields.text: Set each time a received message is stored in a dedicated Receive Buffer.

values.text: One or more received messages stored in a Receive Buffer.

fields.name: TOO
fields.text: Interrupt flag: timeout reached.

fields.name: MRAF
fields.text: Message RAM access failure. Set when the Rx Handler either has not finished acceptance filtering or storing an accepted message by the time the next message's arbitration field is received (it then drops that work and moves to the next message), or could not write a message to the Message RAM (storing is dropped). Either way the FIFO put index stays where it was or the dedicated Receive Buffer's New Data flag stays clear, and the next message stored there overwrites the partial one. Also set when the Tx Handler failed to fetch a message from the Message RAM soon enough; the transmission is dropped and the MCAN enters Restricted Operation mode, which the processor leaves by clearing MCAN_CCCR.ASM.

values.text: A Message RAM access failure occurred.

fields.name: TSW
fields.text: Interrupt flag: wrap around of the timestamp counter.

fields.name: TEFL
fields.text: Interrupt flag: loss of a Tx Event FIFO element.

values.text: An element was lost; also set by a write attempt to a Tx Event FIFO of size zero.

fields.name: TEFF
fields.text: Interrupt flag: Tx Event FIFO full.

fields.name: TEFW
fields.text: Interrupt flag: Tx Event FIFO fill level at its watermark.

fields.name: TEFN
fields.text: Interrupt flag: new entry in the Tx Event FIFO.

values.text: The Tx Handler wrote an element.

fields.name: TFE
fields.text: Interrupt flag: Tx FIFO empty.

fields.name: TCF
fields.text: Interrupt flag: cancellation of a transmission finished.

fields.name: TC
fields.text: Interrupt flag: transmission completed.

fields.name: HPM
fields.text: Interrupt flag: high priority message received.

fields.name: RF1L
fields.text: Interrupt flag: loss of a Receive FIFO 1 message.

values.text: A message was lost; also set by a write attempt to a Receive FIFO 1 of size zero.

fields.name: RF1F
fields.text: Interrupt flag: Receive FIFO 1 full.

fields.name: RF1W
fields.text: Interrupt flag: Receive FIFO 1 fill level at its watermark.

fields.name: RF1N
fields.text: Interrupt flag: new message in Receive FIFO 1.

fields.name: RF0L
fields.text: Interrupt flag: loss of a Receive FIFO 0 message.

values.text: A message was lost; also set by a write attempt to a Receive FIFO 0 of size zero.

fields.name: RF0F
fields.text: Interrupt flag: Receive FIFO 0 full.

fields.name: RF0W
fields.text: Interrupt flag: Receive FIFO 0 fill level at its watermark.

fields.name: RF0N
fields.text: Interrupt flag: new message in Receive FIFO 0.

registers.name: MCAN_RXF0C

fields.name: F0OM

registers.name: MCAN_RXESC
registers.title: MCAN Receive Buffer / FIFO Element Size Configuration
notes: Writes take effect only with both CCE and INIT set to 1 in MCAN_CCCR.
Sets the number of data bytes in each Receive Buffer and Receive FIFO element; sizes over 8 bytes are meant for CAN FD only.
When an accepted frame carries more data than the matching Receive Buffer or Receive FIFO element holds, only the configured number of bytes is stored and the rest of the data field is dropped.

fields.name: RBDS
fields.text: Size of the data field in each Receive Buffer element.

fields.name: F1DS
fields.text: Size of the data field in each Receive FIFO 1 element.

fields.name: F0DS
fields.text: Size of the data field in each Receive FIFO 0 element.

registers.name: MCAN_TXBC
registers.title: MCAN Tx Buffer Configuration
notes: Writes take effect only with both CCE and INIT set to 1 in MCAN_CCCR.
TFQS plus NDTB must not exceed 32; a wrong setting is not caught.
The dedicated Tx Buffers come first in the Message RAM's Tx Buffers section.

fields.name: TFQM
fields.text: Selects Tx FIFO or Tx Queue.

fields.name: TFQS
fields.text: Number of Tx Buffers given to the Tx FIFO/Queue; values over 32 count as 32.

fields.name: NDTB
fields.text: Number of dedicated Tx Buffers; values over 32 count as 32.

fields.name: TBSA
fields.text: Start of the Tx Buffers section in the Message RAM, as a 32-bit word address; bits [15:2] of the address go here.

registers.name: MCAN_TXFQS
registers.title: MCAN Tx FIFO/Queue Status
notes: The status follows the pending requests in MCAN_TXBRP, so an add or cancel request may show late while a Tx scan is running and MCAN_TXBRP has not yet changed.

When dedicated Tx Buffers are mixed with a Tx FIFO or Tx Queue, the Put and Get indices number Tx Buffers from the first dedicated one: with 12 dedicated buffers and a 20-buffer Tx FIFO, Put Index 15 is the Tx FIFO's fourth buffer.

fields.name: TFQF
fields.text: Tx FIFO/Queue full.

fields.name: TFQPI
fields.text: Write pointer of the Tx FIFO/Queue, 0 to 31.

fields.name: TFGI
fields.text: Read pointer of the Tx FIFO, 0 to 31; reads 0 with Tx Queue operation (MCAN_TXBC.TFQM = 1).

fields.name: TFFL
fields.text: Count of free Tx FIFO elements in a row from TFGI, 0 to 32; reads 0 with Tx Queue operation (MCAN_TXBC.TFQM = 1).

registers.name: MCAN_TXESC
registers.title: MCAN Tx Buffer Element Size Configuration
notes: Writes take effect only with both CCE and INIT set to 1 in MCAN_CCCR.
Sets the number of data bytes in each Tx Buffer element; sizes over 8 bytes are meant for CAN FD only.
When an element's DLC asks for more bytes than MCAN_TXESC.TBDS holds, the missing bytes go out as 0xCC padding.

fields.name: TBDS
fields.text: Size of the data field in each Tx Buffer element.

registers.name: MCAN_TXBRP
registers.title: MCAN Transmit Buffer Request Pending
notes: Bits set while a Tx scan runs are left out of that scan; a cancellation requested for such a buffer cancels its add request at once and clears its MCAN_TXBRP bit.

fields.name: TRPx
fields.text: Pending transmission request, one bit per Tx Buffer, only for buffers set up in MCAN_TXBC. Set through MCAN_TXBAR; each setting starts a Tx scan for the highest-priority pending request (the Tx Buffer with the lowest Message ID). Cleared when the transmission completes or is cancelled through MCAN_TXBCR; if the transmission is already under way, a cancellation takes effect at its end, successful or not, and the cancellation request bits clear right after. A finished cancellation then shows in MCAN_TXBCF: after a successful transmission (with the MCAN_TXBTO bit), when the transmission had not started, when arbitration was lost, or when an error occurred in the frame. In DAR mode every unsuccessful transmission is cancelled and its MCAN_TXBCF bit set.

registers.name: MCAN_TXBAR
registers.title: MCAN Transmit Buffer Add Request
notes: An add request for a buffer whose MCAN_TXBRP bit is already set is ignored.

fields.name: ARx
fields.text: Add request, one bit per Transmit Buffer: a 1 sets it, a 0 does nothing, so one write can request several transmissions. Only buffers set up in TXBC take it. With no Transmit scan running the bits clear at once; otherwise they stay set until the scan finishes.

fields.name: CRx
fields.text: Cancellation request, one bit per Transmit Buffer: a 1 sets it, a 0 does nothing, so one write can cancel several. Only buffers set up in TXBC take it. A bit stays set until its MCAN_TXBRP bit clears.

fields.name: TOx
fields.text: Transmission occurred, one bit per Transmit Buffer: set when its MCAN_TXBRP bit clears after a successful transmission, cleared when writing 1 to its MCAN_TXBAR bit requests a new transmission.

fields.name: CFx
fields.text: Cancellation finished, one bit per Transmit Buffer: set when its MCAN_TXBRP bit clears after a cancellation requested through MCAN_TXBCR, or at once if that MCAN_TXBRP bit was not set when cancelled. Cleared when writing 1 to its MCAN_TXBAR bit requests a new transmission.

registers.title: MCAN Transmit Buffer Transmission Interrupt Enable

fields.name: TIEx
fields.text: Transmission interrupt enable, one bit per Transmit Buffer.

registers.name: MCAN_TXBCIE

fields.name: CFIEx
fields.text: Cancellation finished interrupt enable, one bit per Transmit Buffer.

For each bit y of FCLR, where y is the fault input number

registers.name: PWM_FPV1
registers.title: PWM Fault Protection Value Register 1
notes: Writable only while WPSWS5 and WPHWS5 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.

fields.name: FPVLx
fields.text: Level PWML of channel x is forced to on a fault; used only while FPZLx in PWM_FPV2 is 0.

fields.name: FPVHx
fields.text: Level PWMH of channel x is forced to on a fault; used only while FPZHx in PWM_FPV2 is 0.

registers.name: PWM_FPE
registers.title: PWM Fault Protection Enable Register
notes: Writable only while WPSWS5 and WPHWS5 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.
Only bits 7:0 of each field are used, one per fault input pin.

fields.name: FPEx
fields.text: One bit per fault input y: lets fault y trigger the fault protection of channel x. Set a bit only after the matching FPOL bit in PWM_FMR holds its final value, or the protection may trip unexpectedly.

values.when: For each bit y of FPEx, where y is the fault input number
values.text: Fault y does not protect channel x.

values.when: For each bit y of FPEx, where y is the fault input number

registers.name: PWM_ELMRx
registers.title: PWM Event Line x Mode Register

fields.name: CSELy
fields.text: Makes a match of comparison y send a pulse on event line x.

values.text: No pulse on a match of comparison y.
Pulse on event line x at each match of comparison y.

registers.name: PWM_SSPR
registers.title: PWM Spread Spectrum Register
notes: Writable only while WPSWS3 and WPHWS3 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.
Only bits 15:0, the size of the channel counter, are used.

fields.name: SPRDM
fields.text: Chooses how the spread spectrum counter moves.

values.text: Triangular: counts up each PWM period from -SPRD, starting when channel 0 is enabled, and goes back to -SPRD after reaching +SPRD.
Random: takes a new random value, evenly spread between -SPRD and +SPRD, each PWM period.

fields.name: SPRD
fields.text: Limit of the spread spectrum counter, which runs between -SPRD and +SPRD and makes the PWM period vary steadily.

registers.name: PWM_SSPUP
registers.title: PWM Spread Spectrum Update Register
notes: Writable only while WPSWS3 and WPHWS3 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.
Holds a pending SPRD value, so that changing the spread spectrum limit does not disturb the waveform.
Only bits 15:0, the size of the channel counter, are used.

fields.name: SPRDUP
fields.text: New spread spectrum limit SPRD: the counter's range, which makes the period vary steadily.

fields.name: DOWNx
fields.text: Sets the direction of the gray count on channel pair x.

fields.name: GCENx
fields.text: Turns on a gray count on outputs PWML and PWMH 2x and 2x+1.

values.text: Gray count off on PWML/PWMH 2x and 2x+1.
Gray count on, on PWML/PWMH 2x and 2x+1.

registers.name: PWM_FPV2
registers.title: PWM Fault Protection Value Register 2
notes: Writable only while WPSWS5 and WPHWS5 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.

fields.name: FPZLx
fields.text: Puts PWML of channel x in high impedance on a fault, in place of the FPVLx level.

values.text: On a fault, driven to the FPVLx level of PWM_FPV1.

fields.name: FPZHx
fields.text: Puts PWMH of channel x in high impedance on a fault, in place of the FPVHx level.

values.text: On a fault, driven to the FPVHx level of PWM_FPV1.

fields.name: WPKEY
fields.text: Key that must accompany a write of WPCMD.

values.name: PASSWD
values.text: Key "PWM" in ASCII; any other value cancels the WPCMD write. Reads 0.

fields.name: WPRGx
fields.text: Picks register group x as a target of the WPCMD command.

values.text: Group x left alone by WPCMD.

fields.name: WPCMD
fields.text: Write protection action applied to the groups picked in WPRGx; carried out only when WPKEY is 0x50574D.

values.name: DISABLE_SW_PROT
values.text: Software write protection off for the picked groups.

values.name: ENABLE_SW_PROT
values.text: Software write protection on for the picked groups.

values.name: ENABLE_HW_PROT
values.text: Hardware write protection on for the picked groups; only a hardware reset of the PWM removes it, and while on, the PWM's PIO lines cannot be set up through the PIO interface.

fields.name: WPVSRC
fields.text: Offset of the register a write was attempted on, valid while WPVS is 1.

fields.name: WPHWSx
fields.text: Reads 1 while hardware write protection of register group x is on.

fields.name: WPVS
fields.text: Set when a write protection violation has happened; cleared by reading PWM_WPSR.

values.text: No violation since PWM_WPSR was last read.
One or more violations since PWM_WPSR was last read; for a write to a protected register, WPVSRC holds its offset.

fields.name: WPSWSx
fields.text: Reads 1 while software write protection of register group x is on.

registers.name: PWM_CMPVx
registers.title: PWM Comparison x Value Register
notes: Only bits 15:0 of CV, the size of the channel counter, are used.

fields.name: CVM
fields.text: Chooses whether comparison x is made while the channel 0 counter counts up or down.

values.text: Compared while the channel 0 counter rises.
Compared while the channel 0 counter falls; meaningless when channel 0 is left-aligned (CALG = 0 in PWM_CMRx).

fields.name: CV
fields.text: Value that comparison x checks the channel 0 counter against.

registers.name: PWM_CMPVUPDx
registers.title: PWM Comparison x Value Update Register
notes: Holds pending CV and CVM values, so that comparison x does not match unexpectedly.
Only bits 15:0 of CVUPD are used.
PWM_CMPMUPDx is to be written after each write of this register.

fields.name: CVMUPD
fields.text: New CVM: whether comparison x is made while the channel 0 counter counts up or down; meaningless when channel 0 is left-aligned (CALG = 0 in PWM_CMRx).

values.text: Compared while the channel 0 counter rises.
Compared while the channel 0 counter falls.

fields.name: CVUPD
fields.text: New CV: the value comparison x checks the channel 0 counter against.

fields.name: CUPRCNT
fields.text: Current count of the comparison x update period counter. Read-only.

fields.name: CUPR
fields.text: Spacing of updates of the comparison x mode and value, in CUPR + 1 periods of the channel 0 counter.

fields.name: CPRCNT
fields.text: Current count of the comparison x period counter. Read-only.

fields.name: CPR
fields.text: Top count of CPRCNT; comparison x runs once in each CPR + 1 periods of the channel 0 counter.

fields.name: CTR
fields.text: Count of CPRCNT at which comparison x is made.

fields.name: CEN
fields.text: Turns comparison x on.

registers.name: PWM_CMPMUPDx
registers.title: PWM Comparison x Mode Update Register
notes: Holds pending CEN, CTR, CPR and CUPR values, so that comparison x does not match unexpectedly.

fields.name: CUPRUPD
fields.text: New CUPR: spacing of updates of the comparison x mode and value, in CUPR + 1 periods of the channel 0 counter.

fields.name: CPRUPD
fields.text: New CPR: top count of CPRCNT, so comparison x runs once in each CPR + 1 periods of the channel 0 counter.

fields.name: CTRUPD
fields.text: New CTR: the CPRCNT count at which comparison x is made.

fields.name: CENUPD
fields.text: New CEN: turns comparison x on.

registers.name: PWM_CMRx
registers.title: PWM Channel Mode Register
notes: Writable only while WPSWS2 and WPHWS2 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.

fields.name: PPM
fields.text: Turns on Push-Pull mode for channel x.

fields.name: DTLI
fields.text: Inverts the dead-time PWMLx output.

fields.name: DTHI
fields.text: Inverts the dead-time PWMHx output.

fields.name: DTE
fields.text: Turns on the dead-time generator of channel x.

fields.name: TCTS
fields.text: Chooses what channel x hands the Timer Counter (TC) as its trigger.

fields.name: DPOLI
fields.text: Whether the OCx waveform while channel x is disabled (CHIDx in PWM_SR is 0) follows CPOL or is its inverse.

values.text: Inverse of that set by CPOL.

fields.name: UPDS
fields.text: When a center-aligned channel (CALG = 1) takes written update values; a left-aligned one (CALG = 0) always takes them at the end of the period that follows the write.

values.when: If the PWM period is center-aligned (CALG=1)
values.text: Update takes effect at the next end of the period after the write.

values.when: If the PWM period is center-aligned (CALG=1)
values.text: Update takes effect at the next end of the half period after the write.

fields.name: CES
fields.text: When the counter event (CHIDx in PWM_ISR1) of a center-aligned channel (CALG = 1) happens; a left-aligned one (CALG = 0) has it at the end of the period whatever CES holds.

values.when: If the PWM period is center-aligned (CALG=1)
values.text: Counter event at the end of the period only.

values.when: If the PWM period is center-aligned (CALG=1)
values.text: Counter event at the end of the period and at its midpoint.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Level the OCx comparator output starts each period at.

fields.name: CALG
fields.text: Aligns the period of channel x to its left edge or its center.

fields.name: CPRE
fields.text: Clock for the channel x counter. 0: peripheral clock (MCK). 1 to 10 (MCK_DIV_2 to MCK_DIV_1024): peripheral clock divided by 2 to the power of the code. 11: CLKA. 12: CLKB.

registers.name: PWM_CDTYx
registers.title: PWM Channel Duty Cycle Register
notes: Only bits 15:0, the size of the channel counter, are used.

fields.name: CDTY
fields.text: Duty-cycle of the waveform; from 0 up to CPRD in PWM_CPRDx.

registers.name: PWM_CDTYUPDx
registers.title: PWM Channel Duty Cycle Update Register
notes: Holds a pending CDTY value, so that changing the duty-cycle does not disturb the waveform.
Only bits 15:0 are used.

fields.name: CDTYUPD
fields.text: New duty-cycle of the waveform; from 0 up to CPRD in PWM_CPRDx.

registers.name: PWM_CPRDx
registers.title: PWM Channel Period Register
notes: Writable only while WPSWS3 and WPHWS3 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.
Only bits 15:0, the size of the channel counter, are used.

fields.name: CPRD
fields.text: Period of channel x. Left-aligned: X × CPRD / f(peripheral clock), where X is the prescaler 1 to 1024 in powers of two; with CLKA or CLKB, X × CPRD × DIVA / f or X × CPRD × DIVB / f. Center-aligned: twice those, 2 × X × CPRD / f, 2 × X × CPRD × DIVA / f or 2 × X × CPRD × DIVB / f.

registers.name: PWM_CPRDUPDx
registers.title: PWM Channel Period Update Register
notes: Writable only while WPSWS3 and WPHWS3 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.
Holds a pending CPRD value, so that changing the period does not disturb the waveform.
Only bits 15:0 are used.

fields.name: CPRDUPD
fields.text: New CPRD: the period of channel x. Left-aligned: X × CPRDUPD / f(peripheral clock), X being the prescaler 1 to 1024 in powers of two, or with CLKA or CLKB X × CPRDUPD × DIVA / f or X × CPRDUPD × DIVB / f. Center-aligned: twice those.

registers.name: PWM_CCNTx
registers.title: PWM Channel Counter Register
notes: Only bits 15:0, the size of the channel counter, are used.

fields.name: CNT
fields.text: Count of the channel x counter; reset when the channel is enabled by CHIDx in PWM_ENA, and, when left-aligned, when it reaches CPRD in PWM_CPRDx.

registers.name: PWM_DTx
registers.title: PWM Channel Dead Time Register
notes: Writable only while WPSWS4 and WPHWS4 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.
Only bits 11:0 of DTH and DTL, the size of the dead-time counter, are used.

fields.name: DTL
fields.text: Dead-time on the PWMLx output; from 0 up to CDTY in PWM_CDTYx.

fields.name: DTH
fields.text: Dead-time on the PWMHx output; from 0 up to CPRD − CDTY (PWM_CPRDx, PWM_CDTYx).

registers.name: PWM_DTUPDx
registers.title: PWM Channel Dead Time Update Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000000.
Writable only while WPSWS4 and WPHWS4 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.
Holds pending DTH and DTL values, so that changing the dead-times does not disturb the waveform.
Only bits 11:0 of DTHUPD and DTLUPD are used.

fields.name: DTLUPD
fields.text: New dead-time on PWMLx, from 0 up to CDTY in PWM_CDTYx; takes effect when the next channel x PWM period starts.

fields.name: DTHUPD
fields.text: New dead-time on PWMHx, from 0 up to CPRD − CDTY (PWM_CPRDx, PWM_CDTYx); takes effect when the next channel x PWM period starts.

registers.name: PWM_CMUPDx
registers.title: PWM Channel Mode Update Register
notes: Writable only while WPSWS2 and WPHWS2 in PWM_WPSR are both 0.
Holds a pending CPOL value, so that changing the polarity does not disturb the waveform.

fields.name: CPOLINVUP
fields.text: Write 1 to invert the OCx comparator output; a CPOLUP written along with it is then ignored.

fields.text: New CPOL: the level OCx starts each period at; ignored unless CPOLINVUP is written 0 in the same write.

fields.name: RFEN
fields.text: Lets TRGINx raise a recoverable fault in place of fault input x.

values.text: TRGINx raises a recoverable fault, replacing fault input x.

fields.name: TRGSRC
fields.text: Chooses what drives TRGINx.

values.text: Pin PWMEXTRGy: PWMEXTRG0 drives trigger 1 and PWMEXTRG1 drives trigger 2.

fields.name: TRGFILT
fields.text: Turns on filtering of external trigger input x.

fields.name: TRGEDGE
fields.text: Edge or active level of TRGINx; which of the two depends on TRGMODE.

values.name: FALLING_ZERO
values.text: TRGMODE 1: falling edge. TRGMODE 2 or 3: active low.

values.name: RISING_ONE
values.text: TRGMODE 1: rising edge. TRGMODE 2 or 3: active high.

fields.name: TRGMODE
fields.text: Chooses what the external trigger does to channel x.

fields.name: MAXCNT
fields.text: Largest channel x count seen at a TRGINx event since this register was last read; each event replaces it when the count is higher.

fields.name: PWMHREN
fields.text: Turns on leading-edge blanking at rising edges of PWMHx.

fields.name: PWMHFEN
fields.text: Turns on leading-edge blanking at falling edges of PWMHx.

fields.name: PWMLREN
fields.text: Turns on leading-edge blanking at rising edges of PWMLx.

fields.name: PWMLFEN
fields.text: Turns on leading-edge blanking at falling edges of PWMLx.

fields.name: LEBDELAY
fields.text: Blanking time on external trigger input x: LEBDELAY = f(peripheral clock) × Delay + 1.

fields.name: START
fields.text: Write 1 to start an AFE conversion.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to reset the AFEC as a hardware reset would.

registers.name: AFEC_MR
registers.title: AFEC Mode Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x30000000.
Writable only while AFEC_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: USEQ
fields.text: Picks the order in which channels are converted.

values.name: NUM_ORDER
values.text: Channels converted in ascending number order.

values.name: REG_ORDER
values.text: Channels converted in the order set in AFEC_SEQ1R and AFEC_SEQ2R.

fields.name: TRANSFER
fields.text: Number of ADC clock periods from a start command to the selection of the analog channel.

values.text: 8 AFE clocks; recommended for the best conversion.

fields.name: TRACKTIM
fields.text: Tracking time; fixed at 15 AFE clock cycles, so leave this field unchanged.

fields.name: ONE
fields.text: Write 1 to this bit.

fields.name: STARTUP
fields.text: AFE start-up time, in AFE clock periods.

fields.name: PRESCAL
fields.text: Divider from the peripheral clock to the AFE clock: PRESCAL = f(peripheral clock) / f(AFE clock) - 1. At 0 no conversion takes place.

fields.name: FREERUN
fields.text: Free-run mode: converts without waiting for a trigger.

values.name: ON
values.text: Free-run mode; no trigger is awaited.

fields.name: FWUP
fields.text: Fast wake-up between conversions.

values.name: OFF
values.text: Normal sleep; SLEEP sets the sleep mode.

values.name: ON
values.text: Fast wake-up sleep: voltage reference stays on and the AFE is off between conversions.

fields.name: SLEEP
fields.text: Whether the AFE and reference circuits stay powered between conversions.

values.name: NORMAL
values.text: AFE and reference stay on between conversions.

values.name: SLEEP
values.text: AFE and reference are off between conversions.

fields.name: TRGSEL
fields.text: Selects the hardware trigger source.

values.name: AFEC_TRIG0
values.text: AFE0_ADTRG on AFEC0; AFE1_ADTRG on AFEC1.

values.name: AFEC_TRIG1
values.text: Timer Counter channel 0 TIOA on AFEC0; channel 3 TIOA on AFEC1.

values.name: AFEC_TRIG2
values.text: Timer Counter channel 1 TIOA on AFEC0; channel 4 TIOA on AFEC1.

values.name: AFEC_TRIG3
values.text: Timer Counter channel 2 TIOA on AFEC0; channel 5 TIOA on AFEC1.

values.name: AFEC_TRIG4
values.text: PWM0 event line 0 on AFEC0; PWM1 event line 0 on AFEC1.

values.name: AFEC_TRIG5
values.text: PWM0 event line 1 on AFEC0; PWM1 event line 1 on AFEC1.

fields.name: TRGEN
fields.text: Enables the hardware trigger chosen by TRGSEL.

values.name: DIS
values.text: Hardware triggers off; conversions start only from software.

values.name: EN
values.text: Trigger chosen by TRGSEL is on.

registers.name: AFEC_EMR
registers.title: AFEC Extended Mode Register
notes: Writable only while AFEC_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: SIGNMODE
fields.text: Sets whether single-ended and differential results are signed. A signed result under 16 bits is sign-extended to bit 15 (12-bit 0xF43 reads 0xFF43, 0x467 reads 0x0467).

fields.name: STM
fields.text: Single trigger mode for averaged results.

values.text: Several triggers needed for one averaged result.
One trigger gives an averaged result.

fields.name: TAG
fields.text: Adds the channel number to the result read from AFEC_LCDR.

values.text: Channel number is placed with the result in AFEC_LCDR.

fields.name: RES
fields.text: Result resolution and averaging.

values.name: NO_AVERAGE
values.text: 12 bits; full AFE sample rate, no averaging.

values.name: LOW_RES
values.text: 10 bits; full AFE sample rate, no averaging.

values.name: OSR4
values.text: 13 bits; sample rate divided by 4, averaged.

values.name: OSR16
values.text: 14 bits; sample rate divided by 16, averaged.

values.name: OSR64
values.text: 15 bits; sample rate divided by 64, averaged.

values.name: OSR256
values.text: 16 bits; sample rate divided by 256, averaged.

fields.name: CMPFILTER
fields.text: The comparison flag is raised after CMPFILTER + 1 consecutive compare events; at 0 it rises on the first event.

fields.name: CMPALL
fields.text: Compares every channel instead of one.

values.text: Only the channel in CMPSEL is compared.

fields.name: CMPSEL
fields.text: Channel to compare while CMPALL is 0; ignored while CMPALL is 1.

fields.name: CMPMODE
fields.text: Condition that raises a comparison event.

values.name: LOW
values.text: Event when the result is below the window low threshold.

values.name: HIGH
values.text: Event when the result is above the window high threshold.

values.name: IN
values.text: Event when the result is inside the window.

values.name: OUT
values.text: Event when the result is outside the window.

registers.name: AFEC_SEQ2R

notes: Writable only while AFEC_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.name: USCH11
fields.text: Channel number y (0 to 11) converted at step x of the user sequence; only CH0 to CH11 can be sequenced. Takes effect only with AFEC_MR.USEQ set and AFEC_CHSR.CHx set; otherwise the step adds nothing. The same channel in several steps is sampled several times, in a row or not.

fields.name: USCH10
fields.text: Channel number y (0 to 11) converted at step x of the user sequence; only CH0 to CH11 can be sequenced. Takes effect only with AFEC_MR.USEQ set and AFEC_CHSR.CHx set; otherwise the step adds nothing. The same channel in several steps is sampled several times, in a row or not.

fields.name: USCH9
fields.text: Channel number y (0 to 11) converted at step x of the user sequence; only CH0 to CH11 can be sequenced. Takes effect only with AFEC_MR.USEQ set and AFEC_CHSR.CHx set; otherwise the step adds nothing. The same channel in several steps is sampled several times, in a row or not.

fields.name: USCH8
fields.text: Channel number y (0 to 11) converted at step x of the user sequence; only CH0 to CH11 can be sequenced. Takes effect only with AFEC_MR.USEQ set and AFEC_CHSR.CHx set; otherwise the step adds nothing. The same channel in several steps is sampled several times, in a row or not.

registers.name: AFEC_CHER

notes: Writable only while AFEC_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

notes: Writable only while AFEC_WPMR.WPEN is 0.

fields.text: Write 1 to disable channel x. Disabling a channel, or disabling and re-enabling it, mid-conversion makes its data unpredictable, along with its AFEC_ISR.EOCx, AFEC_ISR.GOVRE and AFEC_OVER.OVREx flags.

fields.text: Write 1 to enable the general overrun error interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the data ready interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EOCx

fields.name: GOVRE
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the general overrun error interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the data ready interrupt; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EOCx
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the end-of-conversion interrupt of channel x; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TEMPCHG

fields.name: COMPE

fields.name: GOVRE
fields.text: Reads 1 while the general overrun error interrupt is enabled, 0 while disabled.

fields.name: DRDY
fields.text: Reads 1 while the data ready interrupt is enabled, 0 while disabled.

fields.name: EOCx
fields.text: Reads 1 while the end-of-conversion interrupt of channel x is enabled, 0 while disabled.

fields.name: TEMPCHG
fields.text: Temperature change flag; cleared when AFEC_ISR is read.

values.text: No AFEC_TEMPCMPR comparison match since AFEC_ISR was last read.
The temperature result in AFEC_CDR (AFEC_CSELR.CSEL = 11) changed since AFEC_ISR was last read, by the rules in AFEC_TEMPMR and AFEC_TEMPCWR.

fields.name: COMPE
fields.text: Comparison error flag; cleared when AFEC_ISR is read.

One or more comparison errors since AFEC_ISR was last read.

fields.name: GOVRE
fields.text: General overrun error flag; cleared when AFEC_ISR is read.

registers.name: AFEC_CGR

fields.name: KEYW
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the cryptographic key; four, six or eight of these registers hold a 128-, 192- or 256-bit key, AES_KEYWR0 being the first word and AES_KEYWR3, AES_KEYWR5 or AES_KEYWR7 the last. Writing a new key automatically generates the GCM hash subkey and clears AES_GHASHRx. Write-only, so the key cannot be read back by another application.

fields.name: IDATA
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the 128-bit block to encrypt or decrypt; AES_IDATAR0 holds the first word, AES_IDATAR3 the last. Write-only, so the input cannot be read back by another application.

fields.name: ODATA
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the 128-bit encrypted or decrypted result; AES_ODATAR0 holds the first word, AES_ODATAR3 the last.

fields.name: IV
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the 128-bit initialization vector, an extra starting input for some modes; AES_IVR0 holds the first word, AES_IVR3 the last. In CBC, OFB and CFB it is the initialization vector; in CTR it is the starting counter value. Unused in ECB, where it must not be written. Write-only, so it cannot be read back by another application.

registers.name: AES_AADLENR
registers.title: AES Additional Authenticated Data Length Register

fields.name: AADLEN
fields.text: Number of bytes of additional authenticated data (AAD) to process; the AAD length is bounded by the 32-bit counter.

fields.name: CLEN
fields.text: Number of bytes of plaintext or ciphertext to process; this length is bounded by the 32-bit counter.

registers.name: AES_GHASHRx
registers.title: AES GCM Intermediate Hash Word Register x

fields.name: GHASH
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the intermediate GHASH value. Reading the four words saves the GHASH state so processing can resume later, for instance on a later fragment of a message. Writing a new key generates the GCM hash subkey and clears these registers. A software-chosen GHASH starting value is written here after any key write and before input data begins.

registers.name: AES_TAGRx
registers.title: AES GCM Authentication Tag Word Register x

fields.name: TAG
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the final 128-bit GCM authentication tag, valid once GCM processing ends; TAG0 holds the first word, TAG3 the last.

registers.name: AES_CTRR
registers.title: AES GCM Encryption Counter Value Register

fields.name: CTR
fields.text: Current value of the 32-bit GCM counter.

registers.name: AES_GCMHRx
registers.title: AES GCM H Word Register x

fields.name: H
fields.text: One 32-bit word of the 128-bit GCM hash subkey H. Writing a new key generates H automatically and clears AES_GHASHRx; software may overwrite H here to choose the subkey used for GHASH or to supply one operand of a single GF128 multiply.
